english_literal: [Back to text]
notes: . Previous Contents Next

yoruba: Wèrè èèyàn ní ńwípé irú òun ò sí; irú ẹ̀ẹ́ pọ̀ ó ju ẹgbàágbèje lọ.
english_literal: Only an imbecile asserts that there is none like him or her; his or her likes are numerous, numbering more than millions.
interpretation_gold: No one is incomparable.

yoruba: Wọ́n ńpe gbẹ́nàgbẹ́nà ẹyẹ àkókó ńyọjú.
english_literal: The call goes out for a carpenter and the woodpecker presents itself.
interpretation_gold: One should not think too much of one's capabilities.
notes: . Previous Contents

yoruba: “Yan àkàrà fún mi wá ká jìjọ jẹ ẹ́”: àìtó èèyàn-án rán níṣẹ́ ní ńjẹ́ bẹ́ẹ̀.
english_literal: “Go buy bean fritters for me so we can eat them together”: that spells uncertainly about one's right to send the person concerned on an errand.
interpretation_gold: People in authority should not be tentative in asserting their authority.

yoruba: Yíyẹ́ là ńyẹ́ Òkóró sí tí à ńpè é nígi obì; obì tí ì bá so lórí ẹ̀ ní ńya abidún.
It is only a mark of respect when one calls Òkóró a kolanut tree; any kolanut that might grow on his head would turn out to be slimy.
english_literal: (People who enjoy the respect of others should not make the mistake of overestimating their importance.)
notes: . Contents

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A bímọ kò gbọ́n, a ní kó má ṣàá kú; kí ní ńpa ọmọ bí àìgbọ́n?
english_literal: A child lacks wisdom, and some say that what is important is that the child does not die; what kills more surely than lack of wisdom?
interpretation_gold: A foolish child is not much better than a dead child.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A dẹ́bọ fún igúnnugún, ó ní òun kò rú; a dẹ́bọ fún àkàlà, ó ní òun kò rú; a dẹ́bọ fún ẹyẹlé, ẹyẹlé gbẹ́bọ, ó rúbọ.
english_literal: A sacrifice was prescribed for the vulture, but it refused to sacrifice; a sacrifice was prescribed for the ground-hornbill, but it declined to sacrifice; a sacrifice was prescribed for the pigeon, and it gathered the prescribed materials and made the sacrifice.
interpretation_gold: The vulture and the ground-hornbill are unfortunate in comparison with the pigeon, because they did not carry out the prescribed sacrifice.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A fọwọ́ mú ajá o lọ, a ṣẹ̀ṣẹ̀ ńfi ìka méjì pè é.
english_literal: We grab a dog with the hands and it escapes; thereafter we beckon it with two fingers.
interpretation_gold: If both hands cannot detain a dog, two fingers from a distance will not bring it to where it escaped from.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A fún ọ lọ́bẹ̀ o tami si; o gbọ́n ju ọlọ́bẹ̀ lọ.
english_literal: You are given some stew and you add water; you must be wiser than the cook.
interpretation_gold: Adding water is a means of stretching stew. A person who thus stretches the stew he or she is given would seem to know better than the person who served it how much would suffice for the meal.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í bọ́ sínú omi tán ká máa sá fún òtútù.
english_literal: One does not enter into the water and then run from the cold.
interpretation_gold: Precautions are useful only before the event.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í dá aró nÍṣokùń àlà là ńlò.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: One does not engage in a dyeing trade in Ìṣokùń people there wear only white.
english_literal: (Wherever one might be, one should respect the manners and habits of the place.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í dá ẹrù ikùn pa orí.
english_literal: One does not weigh the head down with a load that belongs to the belly.
interpretation_gold: Responsibilities should rest where they belong.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í du orí olórí kí àwòdì gbé tẹni lọ.
english_literal: One does not fight to save another person's head only to have a kite carry one's own away.
interpretation_gold: One should not save other's at the cost of one's own safety.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í duni lóyè ká fọ̀nà ilé-e Baálẹ̀ hanni.
english_literal: One does not compete with another for a chieftaincy title and also show the way to the king's house to the competitor.
interpretation_gold: A person should be treated either as an adversary or as an ally, not as both.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fá orí lẹ́hìn olórí.
english_literal: One does not shave a head in the absence of the owner.
interpretation_gold: One does not settle a matter in the absence of the person most concerned.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi àgbà sílẹ̀ sin àgbà.
english_literal: One does not leave one elder sitting to walk another elder part of his way.
interpretation_gold: One should not slight one person in order to humor another.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi àì-mọ̀-wẹ̀ mòòkùn.
english_literal: One does not dive under water without knowing how to swim.
interpretation_gold: Never engage in a project for which you lack the requisite skills.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ara ẹni ṣe oògun alọ̀kúnná.
english_literal: One does not use oneself as an ingredient in a medicine requiring that the ingredients be pulverized.
interpretation_gold: Self-preservation is a compulsory project for all.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi aṣọ ṣèdìdí yọwó.
english_literal: One does not leave cloth in a bundle while bargaining over it.
interpretation_gold: It is wise to know what one is negotiating to buy.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ejò sórí òrùlé sùn.
english_literal: One does not go to bed while a snake is on the roof.
interpretation_gold: Never let down your guard while danger still lurks.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Compare A kì í fi iná . . .

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ẹ̀jẹ̀ ìbálé pa tírà; alákoto ò bí abo ọmọ.
english_literal: One does not smear blood (from a woman's deflowering) on a Muslim charm; a de-virgined woman does not give birth to a “female” child.
interpretation_gold: One must not do the forbidden if one does not expect trouble.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ẹ̀tẹ̀ sílẹ̀ pa làpálàpá.
english_literal: One does not ignore leprosy to treat a rash.
interpretation_gold: More serious problems deserve more immediate attention.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ẹran ikún gbọn ti àgbọ̀nrín nù.
english_literal: One does not brush off antelope meat with squirrel meat.
interpretation_gold: Never prefer something of little value to something of great value.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi idà pa ìgbín.
english_literal: One does not use a sword to kill a snail.
interpretation_gold: Remedies should be commensurate with the problem.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ìgbín sọ̀kò sórìṣà.
english_literal: One does not throw a snail at a god.
interpretation_gold: Service to the worthy should be performed with decorum, not with insult.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi iná sórí òrùlé sùn.
english_literal: One does not go to bed while there is a fire on one's roof.
interpretation_gold: Better take care of problems before relaxing.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Compare A kì í fi ejò . . .

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ìtìjú kárùn.
english_literal: One does not because of shyness expose oneself to a disease.
interpretation_gold: Never be too shy to speak out on your own behalf.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ìyá ẹní dákú ṣeré.
english_literal: One does not as a joke say one's mother has collapsed.
interpretation_gold: Never trifle with serious matters.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ogun dán ẹ̀ṣọ́ wò.
english_literal: One does not tease a warrior by saying there is a war (or an invasion.)
interpretation_gold: Do not play with a loaded and primed gun.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ohun sọ́wọ́ búra.
english_literal: One does not hide something in one's hand and yet swear [that one knows nothing about it].
interpretation_gold: It is foolish to tempt fate; the dishonest exposes himself/herself to the possibility of discovery.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ohun-olóhun tọrẹ bí kò ṣe tẹni.
english_literal: One does not make a gift of someone else's property when it is not one's own.
interpretation_gold: Never be too free with other people's property.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi oko sin fún ìwọ̀fà.
english_literal: One does not hide the farm from the pawned worker.
interpretation_gold: It does not make sense to prevent a servant one has hired from doing what one hired him to do.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi olórí ogun ṣe ìfagun.
english_literal: One does not position the commander of the army at the rear of the column.
interpretation_gold: The best foot is the one to put forward.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi oníjà sílẹ̀ ká gbájúmọ́ alápẹpẹ.
english_literal: One does not leave the person one has a quarrel with and face his lackey.
interpretation_gold: Focus rather on your main problem, not a side-show.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi owó du oyè-e alágbára.
english_literal: One does not rely on money to contest a chieftaincy reserved for the strong.
interpretation_gold: Money won't buy everything.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ọlá jẹ iyọ̀.
english_literal: One does not consume salt according to one's greatness.
interpretation_gold: Too much of a good thing can be dangerous.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ọ̀nà ikùn han ọ̀fun.
english_literal: One does not show the throat the way to the stomach.
interpretation_gold: Do not presume to know better than the expert.
notes: See the following entry.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ọ̀nà odò han ikún.
english_literal: One does not show the squirrel the way to the river.
interpretation_gold: Telling someone what he or she already knows is silly.
notes: See the preceding entry.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ọ̀rọ̀ sílẹ̀ gbọ́ ọ̀rọ̀.
english_literal: One does not ignore one matter to attend to another matter.
interpretation_gold: Every obligation deserves attention.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í gbá ẹni tó yọ̀bẹ mú.
english_literal: One does not grab hold of a person who has pulled a knife.
interpretation_gold: Prudence and caution are imperative in dealing with dangerous people.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í gbé ẹran erin lérí ká máa fẹsẹ̀ wa ihò ìrẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not carry elephant meat on one's head and dig cricket holes with one's big toe.
interpretation_gold: If one is blessed with plenty, one should not keep chasing after trifles.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í gbé odò jiyàn-an ọṣẹ́ hó tàbí kò hó.
english_literal: One does not sit by a river and argue whether the soap will foam or will not foam.
interpretation_gold: Where the claim can be put to the test, verbal argument is foolish.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í gbé ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ sọnù ká tún bèrè-e jàǹto.
english_literal: One does not throw a toad away and inquire after its young.
interpretation_gold: Commiseration after injury is hypocritical.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í gbẹ́ àwòrán gàgàrà ká má fi ọwọ́ ẹ ti nǹkan.
english_literal: One does not carve a tall statue without resting its hand on something.
interpretation_gold: Everybody needs some support.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í gbójú-u fífò lé adìẹ àgàgà; a kì í gbójú-u yíyan lé alágẹmọ.
english_literal: One should not expect flight from the flightless chicken; one should not expect striding from a chameleon.
interpretation_gold: To expect the impossible is to delude oneself.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í gbọ́ ẹjọ́ẹnìkan dájọ́.
english_literal: One does not deliver a verdict after hearing only one side.
interpretation_gold: Justice requires impartiality and a full hearing.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í jẹ “Mo fẹ́rẹ̀-ẹ́” lọ́bẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not eat “I almost” in a stew.
interpretation_gold: What one missed narrowly, one cannot enjoy at all.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í ka igún mọ́ ẹran jíjẹ.
english_literal: One does not list vultures among edible meats.
interpretation_gold: Certain things one does not stoop to do.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í ka ilé òrìṣà kún ìlú.
english_literal: One does not count a god's grove as part of the town.
interpretation_gold: Do not list questionable items as part of your wealth.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í ka oyún inú kún ọmọ ilẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not count a fetus among living children.
interpretation_gold: Never count your chickens before they are hatched.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í ka ọmọ fún òbí.
english_literal: One does not enumerate children for the parents.
interpretation_gold: Do not presume to know better than those most intimately involved.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í kọ ọmọ-ọ́ bí ká sọ ọ́ ní Èwolódé?
english_literal: One does not so resent having a child that one names it What-is-this-that-has-happened?
interpretation_gold: Childbirth is always a happy event.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í léku méjì ká má pòfo.
english_literal: One does not chase two rats and avoid coming up with nothing.
interpretation_gold: Never try to go in two directions at once.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Also Ẹní bá léku méjì á pòfo.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í lọ́mọ lẹ́hin kọ oúnjẹ.
english_literal: One does not have children at one's rear and yet refuse food.
interpretation_gold: No amount of anger or distress should keep one from looking after one's dependents.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í mọ ọkọ ọmọ ká tún mọàlè-e rẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not acknowledge the husband for one's child and also acknowledge her illicit lover.
interpretation_gold: Never betray trust or connive at betraying it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í mú ìbọn tetere.
english_literal: One does not hold a gun carelessly.
interpretation_gold: Always be careful in handling dangerous matters.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í mú oko mú ẹjọ́ kí ọ̀kan má yẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not opt to work on the farm and also opt to go argue one's case and avoid neglecting one or the other.
interpretation_gold: One cannot do two mind-absorbing tasks at once.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Compare A kì í múlé móko . . . and A kì í ṣòwò méjì kẹ́ran má jẹ ọ̀kan.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í mú ọmọ oǹdọ́pọ̀ dè.
english_literal: One does not chain the child of a person who offers too low a price for one's wares.
interpretation_gold: It is not a crime to make an offer that might be unacceptable.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í mú ọmọ òṣì lọ sí Ìlọ́rọ̀.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: One does not take a child destined for poverty to Ìlọ́rọ̀.
english_literal: (A person cannot transcend his/her destiny.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í múlé móko kọ́kan má yẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not devote oneself to the home and devote oneself to the farm and not wind up neglecting one of them.
interpretation_gold: One cannot go in two opposite directions at once.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Compare A kì í mú oko mú ẹjọ́..., And A kì í ṣòwò méjì kẹ́ran má jẹ ọ̀kan.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í ní ẹgbàá nílé wá ẹgbàá ròde.
english_literal: One does not have a thousand cowries (or six pence) at home and go chasing abroad for a thousand cowries.
interpretation_gold: Only the promise of a greater fortune should tempt one to neglect what one already has.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í pa asínwín ilé, nítorí ọjọ́ tí tòde yó bàá wá sílé.
english_literal: One does not kill the imbecile within one's home, because of the day when the one from outside might visit one.
interpretation_gold: One should cultivate one's own madness; one might need it to combat others' madness.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í pa igún, a kì í jẹ igún, a kì í fi igún bọrí.
english_literal: One does not kill the vulture; one does not eat the vulture; one does not offer the vulture as a sacrifice to one's head.
interpretation_gold: Certain behaviors are beyond the pale.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í pé kí òṣìkà ṣe é ká wò ó.
english_literal: One does not dare a wicked person to do his worst.
interpretation_gold: Never tempt evil people to do their evil.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í peni lólè ká máa gbé ọmọ ẹran jó.
english_literal: One does not suffer the reputation of being a thief and yet go seeking to dance with kids (baby goats).
interpretation_gold: It is foolish to behave in ways that will confirm people's evil opinion of one.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í rán ọ̀lẹ wo ojú ọjọ́ àárọ̀.
english_literal: One does not send a shirker to go see what the morning looks like outside.
interpretation_gold: Never rely on the advice of people who have a vested interest in the matter being considered.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í re nísun lọ dà síbú.
english_literal: One does not collect water from a spring to dump in the deep.
notes: (Do not rob the poor to further enrich the wealthy.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í rí adìẹ nílẹ̀ ká da àgbàdo fún ajá.
english_literal: One does not see chickens about and throw one's corn to the dog.
interpretation_gold: Always direct help where it will be appreciated and where it will do some good.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í rí àjẹkù orò.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: No one ever sees the leavings of the god Orò.
english_literal: (What must be consumed must be completely consumed.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í rí bàtá nílẹ̀ ká fẹnu sín in jẹ.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: One does not see a bàtá drum on the ground and use one's mouth to mimic its sound.
english_literal: (Too much talk about a problem is useless when a practical solution has presented itself. One should not make a person's case for him or her when the person is present.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í rí ewé nílẹ̀ ká fọwọ́ fámí.
english_literal: One does not see leaves lying about and scoop up feces with one's bare hand.
interpretation_gold: Take advantage of whatever aids are available to you.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í rí ẹ́ni ranni lẹ́rù ká yọké.
english_literal: One does not find helpers willing to help with one's load and yet sprout a hump on one's back “from carrying too heavy a load”.
interpretation_gold: Always avail yourself of offered help.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í rí ojú ẹkùn ká tọ́ ẹkùn.
english_literal: One does not see the look on a leopard's face and then taunt the leopard.
notes: (It is foolish to needlessly invite disaster on one's own head.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í sá fún àjíà ká dìgbò lu eégún.
english_literal: One does not run from the herald of the masquerader and collide with the masquerader himself.
interpretation_gold: Never court a greater disaster in an attempt to avert a minor one.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í sin àlè kọjá odò; ohun tí ńṣe ọṣẹ́ ò tó ǹkan.
english_literal: One does not walk one's secret lover across a river; the causes of huge disasters are usually insignificant in themselves.
interpretation_gold: If one is engaged in a dangerous venture, one should not also cast discretion to the wind.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í sọ pé abẹ Ọ̀yọ́ mú; nígbà náà ni yó sọ pé bẹ́ẹ̀ ni òun ò tíì pọn.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: One does not tell an Ọ̀yọ́ person that his knife is sharp, for only then will he say he has not even honed it yet.
english_literal: (Offer no braggart any opportunity to resume his bragging.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Compare A kì í yin ará Ìjẹ́mọ̀ pé ó mọ asẹ́-ẹ́ hun . . .

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í sọrọ ìkọ̀kọ̀ lójú olófòófó.
english_literal: One does not discuss secret matters in the presence of a tattler.
interpretation_gold: Be careful with your secrets.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í sùn jẹ́rìí ìdí.
english_literal: One cannot be asleep and also be able to vouch for one's anus.
interpretation_gold: Assert only those things you know for certain.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í ṣe fáàárí ẹ̀ṣẹ́ dídì sọ́mọ adẹ́tẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not flaunt one's ability to make a fist in the face of a leper's child.
interpretation_gold: Never make fun of people because of their affliction.
notes: See also the following entry.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í ṣe fáàárí itọ́ dídà sọ́mọ a-kú-wárápá.
english_literal: One does not drool in jest in the presence of the child of an epileptic.
interpretation_gold: Never make fun of afflicted people by mimicking their affliction.
notes: Compare the preceding entry.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í ṣoore tán ká lóṣòó tì í.
english_literal: One does not do a favor and then camp by it.
interpretation_gold: Having done some good, do not hang around to compel gratitude.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í ṣòwò méjì kẹ́ran má jẹ ọ̀kan.
english_literal: One does not engage in two trades without having one consumed by goats.
interpretation_gold: One cannot effectively manage two enterprises at once.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Compare A kì í mú oko mú ẹjọ́ kí ọ̀kan má yẹ̀, and A kì í múlé móko kọ́kan má yẹ̀.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í ti ojú ogun wẹ́fọ́n.
english_literal: One does not wait until the heat of the battle to start looking for palm-leaf midrib.
interpretation_gold: Always make your preparations well ahead of the event.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í ti ojú on-íka-mẹ́sàn-án kà á.
english_literal: One does not count the fingers of a person who has only nine in his/her presence.
interpretation_gold: One must be discreet in speaking about other people's flaws and deformities.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í tijú bá baálé ilé jẹ akátá; bó bá mú, ìwọ náà a mú tìẹ.
english_literal: One should not be too embarrassed to eat a jackal with one's host; as he helps himself, one also helps oneself.
interpretation_gold: Never be too bashful to adopt the ways of the people among whom you find yourself.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í wá aláṣọ-àlà nísọ̀ elépo.
english_literal: One should not look for a white-clad person in the stall of palm-oil sellers.
interpretation_gold: One should know the likely places to look for whatever one seeks.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í wà nínú ìṣẹ́ ká perin tọrẹ.
english_literal: One does not wallow in poverty and yet kill an elephant for public distribution.
interpretation_gold: Always live according to your circumstances.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í wíjọ́ọ wíwò ká jàre.
english_literal: One does not complain about being looked at and be vindicated.
interpretation_gold: One should not complain that other people are doing what one is also doing.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í yin ọmọdé lójú ara ẹ̀; ìfàsẹ́hìn ní ńkángun ẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not praise a child in his presence; only backsliding results.
interpretation_gold: Children should not be praised too highly; they should always be made aware that they can be even better.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kúnlẹ̀ a pàgbò, alubàtá ní “ojú ò fẹ́rakù”; o fẹ́ bá wọn ṣúpó ni?

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: We kneel and sacrifice a ram, and the bàtá drummer shows reluctance to take his leave. Does he wish to inherit a wife?
english_literal: (One should always know when to take one's leave.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: See A sìnkú tán . . .

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A lé tẹ̀m̀bẹ̀lẹ̀kun jìnnà bí ẹnipé kó bọ́ jù sígbó.
english_literal: One chases conspiracy away, as though one would have it disappear into the bush.
interpretation_gold: No one should want anything to do with conspiracy.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: À nfọ̀tún tẹ́ní, à ńfòsì tú ṣòkòtò, obìnrín ní a kò bá òun gbọ́ tọmọ.
english_literal: One spreads a mat with the right hand while removing one's pants with the left hand; yet the woman complains that one is not helping her quest for a child.
interpretation_gold: Some people are incapable of recognizing and acknowledging favors.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: À ńgba òròmọ adìẹ lọ́wọ́ ikú, ó ní wọn ò jẹ́ kí òun jẹ̀ láàtàn.
english_literal: One struggles to save the chick from certain death, and it complains that one is preventing it from foraging at the dump.
interpretation_gold: Chicks foraging at the dump are easy prey for kites.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: À ńgbèjà Ọ̀jà, Ọ̀já ní ta ní ńjà lẹ́hìnkùlé òun?

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: We fight in defence of Ọ̀jà, and Ọ̀jà asks who is fighting in his backyard.
english_literal: (Some people do not acknowledge or appreciate favors.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A ní ìrókò ni yó pa ọmọdé, ó bojú-wẹ̀hìn; òòjọ́ ní ńjà?

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: One curses a child that ìrókò will kill him, and he glances at his rear; does the curse take effect immediately?
english_literal: (The child obviously does not know that the fact that he does not die immediately in no way invalidates the curse.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A ní kí olókùnrùn ṣe tó, ó ní òun ò lè ṣe tó, tò, tó.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: The invalid is asked to say, “Tó,” and he complains that he cannot keep saying, “Tó, tò, tó.”
english_literal: (He has expended more effort in his refusal than he would have in complying.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A ní kọ́mọ má kùú, o ní kò jọ bàbá kò jọ ìyá.
english_literal: We strive to keep a child from dying, and you say he resembles neither the father nor the mother.
interpretation_gold: The person addressed has his or her priorities reversed.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: “À ńjùwọ́n” ò ṣéé wí lẹ́jọ́; ìjà ìlara ò tán bọ̀rọ̀.
english_literal: “We are driven by envy of them” is a bad case to make; a quarrel spawned by jealousy is not easy to settle.
interpretation_gold: Quarrels whose causes cannot be openly admitted will not readily end.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: À ńkì í, à ńsà á, ó ní òun ò mọ ẹni tó kú; a ní, “Alákàá ẹgbàá, a-biṣu-wọ̀rọ̀-wọ̀rọ̀-lóko, a-bàgbàdo-tàkì-tàkì-lẹ́gàn”; ó ní, “Ọlọ́dẹ ló kú, tàbí ìnájà?”
english_literal: We recite someone's praise names, we intone his attributes, and a person says he does not know who died; we say, “He of the two hundred granaries, he whose yams are plentiful on the farm, he whose corn is abundant in the fields,” and the person asks, “Is the dead person a hunter, or a trader?”
interpretation_gold: A person for whom everything must be spelled out, a person who cannot make deductions from the most obvious hints, is daft indeed.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: À ńkì í, à ńsà á, ó ní òun ò mọ ẹni tó kú; ó ńgbọ́, “Ikú mẹ́rù, Ọ̀pàgá, a-biṣu-ú-ta-bí-òdòdó, a-lábà-ọkà, a-roko-fẹ́yẹ-jẹ”; ó ní, “Àgbẹ̀ ló kú, tàbí ọ̀nájà?”
english_literal: We recite someone's praise names, we intone his attributes, and a person says he does not know who died; he hears, “Death takes a renowned man, a titled man, whose yams spread like petals, who possesses barns of corn, whose fields are a bounty for birds,” and he asks, “Is the dead man a farmer or a trader?”
interpretation_gold: This is a variant of the preceding entry.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: À ńsọ̀rọ̀ elégédé, obìnrín ḿbèrè ohun tí à ńsọ, a ní ọ̀rọ̀ ọkùnrin ni; bí a bá kó elégédé jọ, ta ni yó sè é?
english_literal: We are discussing pumpkins, a woman asks what we are discussing, and we respond that it is men's talk; after we have gathered the pumpkins, who will cook them?
interpretation_gold: The woman, certainly. There is no point in excluding her from a matter that will eventually involve her anyway.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: À ńsọ̀rọ̀ obìnrin, a ní ká sọ́ bàrà ká lọ gbin bàrà sódò; ta ní máa báni pa á?
english_literal: We speak of women and someone suggests that we hedge our words and go plant water melon by the stream; who will help in harvesting it?
interpretation_gold: This is a variant of the preceding entry.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A rí i lójú, a mọ̀ ọ́ lẹ́nu; òṣòwò oṣẹ kì í pọ́n-wọ́-lá.
english_literal: One can tell by looking, and one can tell by taste; a soap seller does not lick her fingers.
interpretation_gold: Soap is recognizable as soap, and anyone who has ever tasted it knows that one does not lick fingers caked with soap. Each trade has its don'ts.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: See Aṣòwòọṣẹ kì í pa owó ńlá.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A ta bàbà, a fowó-o bàbà ra baba.
english_literal: We sell guinea-corn, and with the copper coins we redeem the old man.
interpretation_gold: With what one has one seeks one's goals.
notes: [13] See the following entry.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A ta bàbà a fowó-o bàbà ra bàbà.
english_literal: We sell guinea-corn, and with the guinea-corn money we buy guinea corn.
interpretation_gold: This variant of the previous entry suggests that for all one's efforts and exertions one has not significantly altered one's circumstances.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àbá alágẹmọ lòrìṣà ńgbà.
english_literal: The gods heed what chameleon proposes.
interpretation_gold: One should heed the advice of trusted friends and advisers.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àbá kì í di òtítọ́; ojo ni kì í jẹ́ ká dá a.
english_literal: Plans do not automatically bear fruit; only the faint-hearted do not make plans.
interpretation_gold: While plans may never bear fruit, people should still make them.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Compare Àbá ní ńdi òtítọ́ . . .

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àbá ní ńdi òtítọ́; ojo ni kì í jẹ́ ká da.
english_literal: Attempts result in achievement; it is faint-heartedness that keeps one from making an effort.
interpretation_gold: Without striving, one accomplishes nothing.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Compare: Àbá kì í di òtítọ́ . . .

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àbàtì àlàpà; a bà á tì, a bá a rẹ́.
english_literal: Unfinished abandoned wall: unable to master it, one befriends it.
interpretation_gold: One reconciles oneself to matters one cannot control.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-bayé-jẹ́ kò ṣéé fìdí ọ̀ràn hàn.
english_literal: A treacherous person is not someone to tell profound matters to.
interpretation_gold: One should keep one's secrets from treacherous people.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Abẹ́rẹ́ ò ṣéé gúnyán.
english_literal: A needle cannot be used to make pounded yams.
interpretation_gold: Some tools are inadequate for some tasks.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Abẹ́rẹ́ tó wọnú òkun ò ṣéé wá.
english_literal: A needle that drops into the ocean defies finding.
interpretation_gold: Some tasks are hopelessly impossible to accomplish.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Abiyamọ, kàgbo wàrà; ọjọ́ ńlọ.
english_literal: Nursing mother, make the herbal decoction in good time; the day is waning.
interpretation_gold: Attend to duties in time.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Abiyamọ kì í rìn kó ṣánwọ́ ahá.
english_literal: A nursing mother does not venture away from home without a cup.
interpretation_gold: She must be prepared to nurse the baby.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Abiyamọ́ purọ́ mọ́mọ-ọ rẹ̀ jẹun.
english_literal: The nursing mother lies against her child to secure food.
interpretation_gold: One uses every ruse available to one in the interest of one's well-being.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Abiyamọ́ ṣọwọ́ kòtò lu ọmọ-ọ rẹ̀.
english_literal: A nursing mother cups her palm to strike her child.
interpretation_gold: Discretion is the better part of discipline.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àbọ̀ṣẹ́ kì í ṣe iṣẹ́ òòjọ́; iṣẹ́-ẹ baba ẹni ní ńgbani lọ́jọ́ gan-an.
english_literal: Spare-time work is no profession; it is an assignment from one's father that takes all of one's day.
interpretation_gold: One does not waste one's time on trifles or hobbies.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àbùkún layé gbà.
english_literal: The world accepts only adding on.
interpretation_gold: Supplement rather than deplete.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Adánilóró fagbára kọ́ni.
english_literal: He who disappoints one teaches one to be more resourceful.
interpretation_gold: Once disappointed or injured, one learns to be self-reliant.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Adẹ́tẹ̀ ò gbọdọ̀ dúró de eléépín.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A leper must not wait for a bearer of abrasive leaves (eépín
interpretation_gold: Know your weaknesses.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Adẹ́tẹ̀-ẹ́ ní òún sẹ́ ọ̀ràn kan de àwọn ará ilé òun; ó ní bí òún bá lọ sídàálẹ̀, wọn ò jẹ́ fi kàn-ìn-kàn-ìn òun wẹ̀.
english_literal: The leper says that he trusts his relatives on a certain matter; he says when he goes on a journey, they would not dare use his sponge to wash themselves.
interpretation_gold: People have a knack for skirting dangerous or distasteful situations.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Adìẹ ìrànà ní ńṣíwájú òkú.
english_literal: It is the votive herald-chicken that precedes a dead person.
interpretation_gold: Matters must be attended to in their proper sequence.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Adìẹ ò lè ti ìwòyí sunkún ehín.
english_literal: Chicken cannot at this late date bemoan its lack of teeth.
interpretation_gold: Everything at its proper time.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Adìẹ ò lórúnkún ẹjọ́.
english_literal: A chicken has no knees for cases.
interpretation_gold: One should steer clear of actionable behavior.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Adìẹ́ rí aláásáà, ó pa ìyẹ́ mọ́.
english_literal: The chicken sees the snuff seller and enfolds its wings.
interpretation_gold: When one sees potential danger approaching, one should take precautions.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Adìẹ-odò ò ṣéé bọ ìpọ̀nrí.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Water fowl is no good as a sacrifice to ìpọ̀nrí.
english_literal: (One should use only tools proper to the task in hand.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àdó gba ara ẹ̀ tẹ́lẹ̀, ká tó fi oògùn sí?
english_literal: Could the small gourd save itself, before we put charms into it?
interpretation_gold: Do not seek protection from a helpless person.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-fàtẹ́lẹwọ́-fanná kì í dúró.
english_literal: He-who-carries-live-coals-in-his-palm does not tarry.
interpretation_gold: A person who has a pressing problem has no time for socializing.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-fasẹ́-gbèjò ńtan ara-a rẹ̀ jẹ.
english_literal: He-who-would-collect-rain-water-in-a-sieve deceives himself.
interpretation_gold: The shiftless person hurts himself more than others.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Afẹ́fẹ́ ńda ológìì láàmú; oníyẹ̀fun rọra.
english_literal: The wind is making life difficult for the seller of liquid corn starch; corn flour seller, you had better watch out!
interpretation_gold: When those better situated than one are defeated, one must be prepared for tough times.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àfẹ́ẹ̀rí kan ò ju ká rí igbó ńlá bọ́ sí lọ; ẹbọ kan ò ju ọ̀pọ̀ èèyàn lọ; “Òrìṣá gbé mi lé àtète” kan ò ju orí ẹṣin lọ.
english_literal: There is no disappearing trick better than the availability of a dense forest to disappear into; there is no sacrifice more efficacious than having many people on one's side; there is no “The gods have elevated me” that is higher than the back of a horse.
interpretation_gold: Practical and realistic moves are more reliable than mysterious expectations.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-fi-tiẹ̀-sílẹ̀-gbọ́-tẹni-ẹlẹ́ni, ọ̀gànjọ́ ni wọ́n ńsìnkú-u rẹ̀.
english_literal: He-who-neglects-his-own-affairs-to-care-for-others'-affairs, it is in the middle of the night that his burial is carried out.
interpretation_gold: Do not sacrifice your self-interest to take care of others.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àfòmọ́ ńṣe ara-a rẹ̀, ó ní òún ńṣe igi.
english_literal: The creeper is destroying itself, but it thinks it is destroying its host.
interpretation_gold: The host's death will be the parasite's death.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àgádágodo ò finú han ara-a wọn.
english_literal: Padlocks do not share their secrets with one another.
interpretation_gold: Some secrets one should not divulge to others.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àgùntàn ò jí ní kùtùkùyù ṣe ẹnu bọbọ.
english_literal: A sheep does not wake in the morning and droop its mouth.
interpretation_gold: One should not dawdle in the morning.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àgbà òṣìkà ńgbin ìyà sílẹ̀ de ọmọọ rẹ̀.
english_literal: A wicked elder sows suffering for his children.
interpretation_gold: One's character often affects the fortunes of one's children.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Compare, Àgbà tó gbin èbù ìkà . . .

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àgbà ṣoore má wo bẹ̀.
english_literal: Elder, do a favor and remove your eyes from it.
interpretation_gold: Do not advertize your acts of kindness, or pointedly await acknowledgment of them.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: À-gbà-bọ́ ò di tẹni.
english_literal: A foster child does not become one's own child.
interpretation_gold: There is nothing like having one's own.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Compare Àgbàtọ́ ò jọ obí . . .

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àgbàdo kì í ṣe èèyàn;ta ní ńrí ọmọ lẹ́hìn eèsún?
english_literal: The maize plant is not a human being; who ever saw children on the back of elephant grass?
interpretation_gold: One should not overestimate the value of things.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àgbàká labiyamọ ńgbàjá mọ́ ọmọ-ọ rẹ̀.
english_literal: It is completely and securely that a mother (bearing her child on her back) supports the child with a strip of cloth.
interpretation_gold: One must be thorough in discharging one's responsibility.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: 337. Àgbàlagbàá ṣenú kẹrẹndẹn; èyí tó máa ṣe ḿbẹ níkùn-un rẹ̀.
english_literal: An elder shows a smooth belly to the world; but what he will do is known to him.
interpretation_gold: Be a person of thought and action, not of words.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-gbé-ọ̀ọ̀dẹ̀ bí òfé, a-mọ-ara-í-ré bí oódẹ;a dẹ́bọ fún òfé, òfé ò rú, agánrán gbẹ́bọ, ó rúbọ; àsẹ̀hìnwá àsẹ̀hìnbọ̀ òfé di ará Ọ̀yọ́, agánrán di ará oko; wọ́n rò pé òfé ò gbọ́n.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Òfé, dweller-in-the-corridor, forward as oódẹ́ a sacrifice was prescribed for òfé, but he did not offer it; agánrán went ahead and offered the sacrifice; in the end òfé became a citizen of Ọyọ, while agánrán became a dweller in the bush; and people thought òfé was foolish.
english_literal: (Never second guess people who are better informed than you are.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àgbẹ̀jẹ ò korò nílé ńlá.
english_literal: Pumpkin is never bitter in a big household.
interpretation_gold: When one is in need, one cannot be too choosy.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àgbìgbò, rọra fò, ọdẹ́ ti dé sóko; àgbìgbò tí ò bá rọra fò á bọ́ sápò ọdẹ.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àgbìgbò, fly warily, for the hunter has arrived in the forest; any àgbìgbò that does not fly warily will wind up in the hunter's bag.
english_literal: (Conditions are hazardous; it behooves everyone to take care.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àgbò dúdú kọjá odò ó di funfun.
english_literal: The black ram crosses the river and becomes white.
interpretation_gold: Propitious events can drastically change a person's fortunes for the better.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àgbókan là ńrọ́ Ifá adití.
english_literal: It is with full voice volume that one recites divination verses for the deaf.
interpretation_gold: One cannot be too subtle with the daft.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àgbọn kì í ṣe oúnjẹ ẹyẹ.
english_literal: Coconut is no food for birds.
interpretation_gold: Some things and some people are immune to some types of danger; one should not attempt the impossible.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ahún dùn;kò tóó jẹ fúnni.
english_literal: Tortoise meat is delicious, but there is not enough of it to make a meal.
interpretation_gold: One should husband one's resources wisely.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ahún ńre àjò, ó gbé ilé-e rẹ̀ dání.
english_literal: Tortoise embarks on a journey and takes his house with it.
interpretation_gold: One's dearest possessions deserve one's closest attention.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ahun-ún wọnú orù, ó ku àtiyọ.
english_literal: Tortoise has entered into a narrow-necked pot; now, getting out is a problem.
interpretation_gold: One should consider the possible consequences of one's actions before one acts.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àìgbọ́n ni yó pa Iṣikan; a ní ìyáa rẹ̀-ẹ́ kú, ó ní nígbàtí òún gbọ́, ṣe ni òún ńdárò; bíyàá ẹní bá kú àárò là ńdá?

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Foolishness will be the death of Iṣikań he is told that his mother has died, and he says that when he heard the news he sorely lamented the tragedy; if one's mother dies is it lamentation that is called for?
english_literal: (The well bred person is always mindful of his/her obligations.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àì-gbọ́n-léwe ni à-dàgbà-di-wèrè.
english_literal: Lack-of-wisdom-in-youth is imbecility in adulthood.
interpretation_gold: The man turns out just as the child was; the grown person acquires his traits in childhood.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àì-mọ̀-ọ́-gbé-kalẹ̀ leégún fi ńgba ọtí.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: It is ineptitude-in-setting-it-down that makes the wine a spoil for the eégún (i.e., that causes the wine to be spilled).
english_literal: (Ineptitude makes an impossible job of the easiest tasks.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àì-mọwọ́-ọ́-wẹ̀ ni àì-bágbà-jẹ; ọmọ tó mọwọ́-ọ́ wẹ̀ á bágbà jẹ.
english_literal: Not-knowing-how-to-wash-one's-hands is not-eating-with-elders; a person who knows how to wash his hands will eat with elders.
interpretation_gold: To qualify to live in society, one must learn the social graces.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àìpé, “Tìrẹ nìyí” ní ḿbí ayé nínú.
english_literal: Neglect to say, “Here is your's” is what incites the earth's anger.
interpretation_gold: Failure to take account of people's possible influence on one's affairs incites their anger. As long as one assumes humility, people will let one be.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àì-roko, àì-rodò tí ńṣápẹ́ fún eégún jó.
english_literal: Not-going-to-the-farm, not-going-to-the-river that claps for masqueraders to dance.
interpretation_gold: It is an idler who makes music for masqueraders to dance.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àì-sọ̀rọ̀ ní ńmú ẹnu rùn.
english_literal: It is abstention from speaking that makes the mouth smell.
interpretation_gold: One should always say one's piece in a discussion.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ajá èṣín ò mọdẹ.
english_literal: A dog born a year ago does not know how to hunt.
interpretation_gold: One learns from experience and maturity.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ajá là bá kí; èse ò pẹran fúnni jẹ.
english_literal: One should rather commend the dog; the cat does not kill meat for one to eat.
interpretation_gold: Assign commensurate values to your assets.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ajá tí ò létí ò ṣé-é dẹ̀gbẹ́.
english_literal: A dog without ears is no good for stalking prey.
interpretation_gold: A person who cannot be instructed is useless.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ajá ti eré-e rẹ̀ẹ́ bá dánilójú là ńdẹ sí ehoro.
english_literal: It is a dog in whose speed one has faith that one sics at a hare.
interpretation_gold: One entrusts important tasks only to those one can trust.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: This is a variant of Ajá to lè sáré . . .

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ajá tó gbé iyọ̀, kí ni yó fi ṣe?
english_literal: A dog that swipes salt, what will it do with it?
interpretation_gold: Do not expend your effort on senseless ventures.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ajá tó lè sáré là ńdẹ sí egbin.
english_literal: It is a swift dog that one sends after a Kobe antelope.
interpretation_gold: This is a variant of Ajá ti erée rẹ̀ẹ́ bá dánilójú . . .

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ajàkàṣù ò mọ̀ bí ìyàn-án mú.
english_literal: The person who eats large helpings does not care that there is a famine.
interpretation_gold: Greed knows no thrift.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-jí-má-bọ̀ọ́jú, tí ńfi ojú àná wòran.
english_literal: A-person-who-rises-in-the-morning-without-washing-his-face, one who sees things with yesterday's eyes.
interpretation_gold: A person who does not keep his eyes peeled for developments is ever behind times.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjànàkú kúrò lẹ́ran à ńgọ dé.
english_literal: The elephant is not among the ranks of animals one lies in ambush for.
interpretation_gold: The wise person puts some distance between himself and an elephant, or a formidable adversary.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjànàkú ò ṣéé rù.
english_literal: The elephant is impossible to carry.
interpretation_gold: Some tasks are impossible to accomplish.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjàpá ní kò sí oun tó dà bí oun tí a mọ̀ ọ́ṣe; ó ní bí òún bá ńrìn lóko ẹ̀pà, ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan a máa bọ́ sóun lẹ́nu.
english_literal: Tortoise says there is nothing quite like what one knows how to do; it says when it walks through a peanut farm, peanuts keep popping one by one into its mouth.
interpretation_gold: When one does what one is a true expert at doing, it seems like performing magic.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjàpá ní ọjọ́ tí òún ti jágbọ́n-ọn òo lọrùn ò ti wọ òun mọ́.
english_literal: Tortoise says that since the day it learned the trick of saying yes its neck has ceased to shrink.
interpretation_gold: One who says yes to every request avoids a great many arguments.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: See Ẹlẹ́dẹ̀ẹ́ ní ọjọ́ tí òún ti jágbọ́nọn hùn . . ., and Ẹrùu òo kì í wọni lọ́rùn.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjàpá ńyan lóko, aláìlóye-é ní ó jọ pẹ́pẹ́yẹ.
english_literal: The tortoise struts on the farm, the senseless person says it resembles a duck.
interpretation_gold: It is indeed a fool that cannot discern the obvious.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjẹ́gbà ni ti kọ̀ǹkọ̀.
english_literal: Croaking-in-relays is the mark of frogs.
interpretation_gold: It is in the nature of sheep to follow and to lack initiative.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjẹ́kù là ńmayo.
english_literal: Leaving-remnants is the indicator of satiation.
interpretation_gold: How one lives will show how well off one is.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjẹkù làgbẹ̀ ńtà.
english_literal: It is the leavings from his table that the farmer sells.
interpretation_gold: One takes care of one's needs before one disposes of the excess.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: See, Àjẹkùlóko àgbẹ̀ . . .

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjẹsílẹ̀-ẹ gbèsè tí ò jẹ́ kí ẹgbẹ̀fà tóó ná.
english_literal: Long-standing debt, that makes twelve hundred cowries insufficient to spend.
interpretation_gold: Existing debts eat new fortunes away.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjímú kì í tí.
english_literal: The task one takes on waking in the morning does not flounder.
interpretation_gold: The task to which one gives the highest priority does not suffer.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjò kì í dùn kódídẹ má rèWó.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: The journey is never so pleasant that the parrot does not return to Ìwó.
english_literal: (The sojourner should never allow the pleasantness of his/her sojourn to obliterate thoughts of returning home.)
notes: [35] See the following entry.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjò kì í dùn kónílé má relé.
english_literal: The journey is never so pleasant that the traveler does not return home.
interpretation_gold: The traveler should never forget his or her home.
notes: See the previous entry.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjòjí lójú, ṣùgbọ́n kò fi ríran.
english_literal: A stranger has eyes, but they do not see.
interpretation_gold: A stranger's eyes are blind to the intricacies of his new surroundings.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: À-jókòó-àì-fẹ̀hìntì, bí ẹní nàró ni.
english_literal: Sitting-without-leaning-the-back-against-something is like standing.
interpretation_gold: Never do things by half measures.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àkámọ́ ẹkùn-ún níyọnu.
english_literal: A cornered leopard poses problems.
interpretation_gold: One should be wary of what prey to stalk.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àkísà aṣọ la fi ńṣe òṣùká.
english_literal: A rag is what one uses as a carrying pad.
interpretation_gold: One's most valuable possessions are not for careless use.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àkó balẹ̀, ó fi gbogbo ara kígbe.
english_literal: Àko hit the ground and cried out with its whole body.
interpretation_gold: A person who needs help should not be coy in asking.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-ká-ìgbá-tà-á náwó ikú.
english_literal: He-who-plucks-the-African-locustbean-tree-seeds-to-sell spends death's money.
interpretation_gold: Whoever engages in a dangerous venture more than earns his/her pay.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Akọ̀pẹ Ìjàyè ò gbọ́ tiẹ̀, ó ní ogún kó Agboroode.
english_literal: The palm-wine tapper of Ijaye: instead of looking to his own affairs says Agboroode has been destroyed by invaders.
interpretation_gold: The wise person learns from others' misfortunes instead of gawking at them.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Aláàjàá gbé e sókè, o ní, “Kó ṣẹ!”; o mọ̀ bí ibi lówí tàbí ire?
english_literal: The wielder of the incantation rattle lifts it, and you respond, “May it be so!”; do you know if he has invoked good or evil?
interpretation_gold: One should be certain about what is happening before one intervenes or becomes involved.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Alágbàfọ̀ kì í bá odò ṣọ̀tá.
english_literal: A washerman does enter harbor a grudge with the river.
interpretation_gold: One does not turn one's back on one's means of livelihood.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Alákatam̀pòó ṣe bí ọ̀bọ ò gbọ́n; ọ̀bọ́ gbọ́n; tinú ọ̀bọ lọ̀bọ́ ńṣe.
english_literal: The person with the cross-bow thinks that the monkey is not clever; the monkey is clever, but it is following its own strategy.
interpretation_gold: It matters nothing if one is derided, as long as one knows what one is doing and why.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Alákìísà ní ńtọ́jú abẹ́rẹ́ tòun tòwú.
english_literal: It is the owner of rags who makes sure that needle and thread are available.
interpretation_gold: Each person looks after his/her own interests.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Aláǹtakùn, bí yóò bá ọ jà, a ta ká ọ lára.
english_literal: When the spider wants to engage an enemy, it spins its web around it.
interpretation_gold: The attentive person can detect signs of hostility before it occurs. Also, one makes good preparations before embarking on a venture.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Aláǹtakùnún takùn sí ìṣasùn, ṣíbí gbọludé.
english_literal: The spider has woven its web in the sauce-pan; the spoon takes a holiday.
interpretation_gold: In the absence of the proper tools, one cannot fault the laborer for being idle.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Aláàárù kì í ru ẹṣin.
english_literal: The porter cannot carry a horse.
interpretation_gold: Certain tasks are impossible of accomplishment.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Aláṣedànù tí ńfajá ṣọdẹ ẹja.
english_literal: A wastrel “who” uses a dog to stalk fish.
interpretation_gold: It is folly to employ an impossible tool for a given task.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àlejò bí òkété là ńfi èkùrọ́ lọ̀.
english_literal: It is a visitor like a giant rat to whom one offers palm-nuts.
interpretation_gold: One should approach other people as their stations dictate.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àlejò tó bèèrè ọ̀nà kò níí sọnù.
english_literal: A stranger who asks the way will not get lost.
interpretation_gold: One should be willing to admit one's ignorance and seek direction.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Compare: Abéèrè kì í ṣìnà.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àlùkò ò ní ohùn méjì; “Ó dilé” lagbe ńké.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: The woodcock has but one statement: “Ó dilé” (meaning “Time to head for home”) is the cry of the touraco.
english_literal: (One should know when the time is ripe to head for home.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àlùsì ẹsẹ̀ tí ńfa koríko wọ̀lú.
english_literal: Disaster-causing legs that drag weeds into town.
interpretation_gold: It is a person who will bring disaster on others who behaves like the wayward foot that drags weeds into town.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Amọ̀nà èṣí kì í ṣe amọ̀nà ọdúnnìí.
english_literal: The person who knew the way last year does not necessarily know the way this year.
interpretation_gold: The person whose knowledge does not grow with the times soon becomes ignorant.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Amọ̀rànbini Ọ̀yọ́, bí o bá gbé kete lérí, wọn a ní oko lò ńlọ tàbí odò.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: People who-know-the-answer-yet-ask-the-question, natives of Ọ̀yọ́, if they see you carrying a water-pot they ask whether you are on your way to the farm or the stream.
english_literal: (If the answer is plain to see, one does not ask the question.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Amùṣùà àgbẹ̀ tí ńgbin kókò.
english_literal: A wastrel farmer that plants cocoyams.
interpretation_gold: It is a wastrel farmer that plants cocoyams.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àpà èèyàn ò mọ̀ pé ohun tó pọ̀-ọ́ lè tán.
english_literal: A wastrel does not know that what is plentiful can be used up.
interpretation_gold: A wastrel knows no thrift.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àpà-á fi ọwọ́ mẹ́wẹ̀ẹ̀wá bọ ẹnu; àpà, a-bìjẹun-wọ̀mù-wọ̀mù.
english_literal: The wastrel puts all ten fingers into his mouth; wastrel, a-person-who-eats-with-abandon.
interpretation_gold: A wastrel is immoderate in his feeding.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Apajájẹẹ́ ní ẹ̀rù adìẹ ḿba òun.
english_literal: The-person-who-kills-and-eats-dogs claims to be afraid of chickens.
interpretation_gold: A hardened criminal pretends to have scruples about mere peccadillos.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àpàkòmọ̀rà, tí ńgẹṣin lórí àpáta.
english_literal: A-shiftless-person-who-knows-not-what-things-cost rides a horse on rocks.
interpretation_gold: A person who has no part in paying for a thing is seldom careful in using it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Compare: Ẹni à ḿbọ́ ò mọ̀ pé ìyànán mú.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-pẹ́-ẹ́-jẹ kì í jẹ ìbàjẹ́.
english_literal: A person who waits patiently for a long time before eating will not eat unwholesome food.
interpretation_gold: Those who are patient will have the best of things.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àpèmọ́ra là ńpe Tèmídire.
english_literal: It is in furtherance of one's own fortune that one calls the name Temidire.
interpretation_gold: Each person must advance his or her own interests.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àpọ́n dògí ó ṣàrò.
english_literal: When a bachelor becomes old, he makes his own cooking fire.
interpretation_gold: One should make provisions for the future in one's youth.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ara ẹ̀ lara ẹ̀: ṣòkòtò ọlọ́pàá.
english_literal: A little bit of it is a little bit of it: the policeman's short pants.
interpretation_gold: Leave nothing to waste, for one can always find some use for the smallest remnant.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ara kì í rọni ká ṣẹ́gi ta.
english_literal: If one has the wherewithal to live a life of ease, one does not gather firewood for sale.
interpretation_gold: When one has found success, one does not persist in grubbing.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ara kì í tu ẹni káká, kí ara ó roni koko, ká má leè jíkàkà dÍfá.
english_literal: One cannot be so much at ease, or so much in pain, that one cannot wake early to consult the oracle.
interpretation_gold: Whatever one's condition, one does what one must do.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ará ọ̀run ò ṣẹ́tí aṣọ.
english_literal: Natives of heaven do not sew their hems.
interpretation_gold: The uninitiated do not know the customs of a place.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ààrẹ ńpè ọ́ ò ńdÍfá; bÍfá bá fọọre tí Ààrẹ́ fọbi ńkọ́?

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: The Ààrẹ summons you and you consult the oracle; what if the oracle says all will be well and the Ààrẹ decrees otherwise?
english_literal: (There is no point in attempting to restrict the action of an absolute authority.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-rìn-fàà-lójú-akẹ́gàn, a-yan-kàṣà-lojú-abúni, abúni ò lówó nílé ju ẹnu-u rẹ̀ lọ.
english_literal: One-who-saunters-in-front-of-detractors, one-who-struts-before-abusers, those who abuse one have no money at home, only their mouths.
interpretation_gold: One's best course is to ignore detractors and insulters; all they have is their mouths.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Arìngbẹ̀rẹ̀ ni yó mùú oyè délé; asárétete ò róyè jẹ.
english_literal: The person who walks casually is the one who will bear a title home; the person who runs fast has no title to show for his efforts.
interpretation_gold: The spoils do not necessarily go to those who exert themselves most.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Compare: Asárétete ní ńkọjá ilé . . .

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: À-ró-kanlẹ̀ laṣọ ayaba; à-wà-kanlẹ̀ ni ti yàrà.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Wrapping-from-waist-to-the-floor is the style of the queen's wrapper; digging-down-to-the-deepest-bottom is the requirement of the dry moat, yàrà.
english_literal: (Whatever one has to do, one must be thorough, and not be satisfied with halfmeasures.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Arúgbó oǹdágbèsè, ó ní mélòó ni òun óò dúró san níbẹ̀?
english_literal: The old person who incurs debt, he says how much of it will he be around to pay?
interpretation_gold: A person whose days are numbered can afford to freely take on long-term obligations.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-sáré-lówó ḿbẹ lọ́nà ogun; A-pọ̀ṣẹ̀ṣẹ̀ ḿbẹ lọ́nà èrò; Bó-pẹ́-títí-ng-ó-là ḿbẹ lábà, ó ńjẹ ẹ̀sun iṣu.
english_literal: He-who-hurries-after-riches is on his way to battle; He-who-has-in-abundance is off on his travels; Sooner-or-later-I-will-be-rich is back in his hut, eating roasted yams.
interpretation_gold: Wealth comes to those who exert themselves, not to those who wait for it to find them.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: À-sìnkú-àì-jogún, òṣì ní ńtani.
english_literal: Burying-the-dead-without-sharing-in-the-inheritance leads one to poverty.
interpretation_gold: One should have something to show for one's efforts.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Asínwín ní òun ó ti iná bọlé; wọ́n ní kó má ti iná bọlé; ó ní òun ó sáà ti iná bọlé; wọ́n ní bó bá tiná bọlé àwọn ó sọ ọ́ si; ó ní ìyẹn kẹ̀ ìkan.
english_literal: The imbecile said he would torch the house; he was asked not to torch the house; he said he certainly would torch the house; he was told that if he torched the house he would be thrown in it; he said, “That casts the matter in a different light.”
interpretation_gold: Even an imbecile becomes sane when his life is at stake.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-sọ̀kò-sádìẹ-igba, òkò ní ńsọ tí ilẹ̀-ẹ́ fi ńṣú.
english_literal: One-who-throws-stones-at-two-hundred-chickens will be engaged in stone throwing until nightfall.
interpretation_gold: Tackling a job with inadequate tools makes the job interminable.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-sọ-aré-dìjà ní ńjẹ̀bi ẹjọ́.
english_literal: One-who-turns-play-into-a-fight is always guilty.
interpretation_gold: One should take a jest in the spirit of jest.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àṣàyá kì í jẹ́ kí ọmọ ọ̀yà ó gbọ́n.
english_literal: Roughhousing keeps the young of the cane rat from learning wisdom.
interpretation_gold: A person who takes life as a jest does not learn to be wary.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-ṣe-kó-súni, ẹrú-u Ségbá; ó fọ́ akèrègbè tán ó lọ sóde Ọ̀yọ́ lọ gba onísé wá; bẹ́ẹ̀ni ẹgbàá lowó onísé.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: He-who-frustrates-one, Segba's slave; he broke a gourd and went to Ọ̀yọ́town to hire a calabash stitcher; and a stitcher's fee is six pence.
english_literal: (There is nothing one can do in the face of ingrained folly.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: À-ṣe-sílẹ̀ làbọ̀wábá; ẹni tó ṣu sílẹ̀ á bọ̀ wá bá eṣinṣin.
english_literal: What-is-put-aside is what-is-there-to-find; he who puts excrement aside will return to find flies.
interpretation_gold: One reaps what one sows.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: À-ṣẹ̀ṣẹ̀-tọ́-ọtí-wò okùn-un bàǹtẹ́ já; bí a bá mu àmuyó ńkọ́?
english_literal: One taste of wine and the belt snaps; what would happen in the event of drunkenness?
interpretation_gold: One should match the response to the stimulus.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Aṣiwèrè èèyàn lòjò ìgboro ńpa.
english_literal: It is an imbecile who is soaked in the rain in the middle of a town.
interpretation_gold: Only an imbecile ignores a refuge when one is available.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Aṣiwèrè èèyàn ní ńgbèjà ìlú-u rẹ̀.
english_literal: Only an imbecile gets into a fight in defence of his town.
interpretation_gold: A town's cause is no business of any one individual.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Aṣòroójà bí ìjà ọjà; onítìjú ò níí sá; ẹni tí ńnà án ò níí dáwọ́ dúró.
english_literal: Difficult-to-fight as the fight of the market place; the self-conscious person will not run, and the person beating him up will not stop.
interpretation_gold: Too much concern with appearances exposes one to occasional inconveniences.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-ṣòwò-ọṣẹ kì í pa owó ńla.
english_literal: A trader in soap does not make big money.
interpretation_gold: One's success cannot exceed one's enterprise.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: See A rí i lójú, . . .
