part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-ṣoore-jókòó-tì-í, bí aláìṣe ni.
english_literal: A-person-who-does-a-favor-and-squats-by-it is like a-person-who-has-done-no-favor.
interpretation_gold: One should not dwell on what favor one has done.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Aṣọ funfun òun àbàwọ́n kì í rẹ́.
english_literal: White cloth and stains are not friends.
interpretation_gold: A person of good breeding does not associate with an ill-bred person.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Aṣọ ìrókò ò ṣéé fi bora.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Cloth fashioned from the bark of the ìrókò tree cannot be wrapped around one's body.
english_literal: (Always use the proper material for the job in hand.)

yoruba: Aṣọ tá a bá rí lára igún, ti igún ni.
english_literal: Whatever cloth one finds on the vulture belongs to it.
interpretation_gold: The vulture may lack feathers, but it does not borrow from other birds.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-sọ́-ẹ̀hìnkùlé ba araa rẹ̀ nínú jẹ́; ohun tó wuni là ńṣe nílé ẹni.
english_literal: He-who-spies-on-others-from-behind-their-walls upsets himself; one does as one pleases in one's home.
interpretation_gold: What one does in the privacy of one's home is nobody's business.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àtàrí ìbá ṣe ìkòkò ká gbé e fún ọ̀tá yẹ̀wò; a ní ó ti fọ́ yányán.
english_literal: If one's head was a pot and one gave it to an enemy to inspect, he would say it was irretrievably broken.
interpretation_gold: An enemy is not one to trust with one's destiny.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Atẹ́gùn ò ṣéé gbé.
english_literal: The wind is impossible to carry.
interpretation_gold: Certain propositions are unrealizable.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àtẹ́lẹwọ́ ò ṣéé fi rúná.
english_literal: The palm of the hand is not good for stoking fires.
interpretation_gold: One should not attempt difficult tasks without the proper resources.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Atipo ò mọ erèé; ó ní, “Bàbá, mo réwé funfun lóko.”
english_literal: Atipo does not recognize beans, he says, “Father, I saw white leaves on the farm.”
interpretation_gold: Ignorance is a curse.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àtònímòní ò tó àtànọ́mànọ́.
english_literal: All-day-long is no match for since-yesterday.
interpretation_gold: The person who has endured since yesterday takes precedence over the person who has endured all day.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-tọrọ-ohun-gbogbo-lọ́wọ́-Ọlọ́run kì í kánjú.
english_literal: The-seeker-of-all-things-from-God does not yield to impatience.
interpretation_gold: The supplicant must be patient for an answer.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-wí-fúnni-kó-tó-dáni, àgbà òmùjà ni.
english_literal: He-who-alerts-one-before-he-throws-one is a past master of wrestling.
interpretation_gold: One would be wise to avoid adversaries confident enough to show their hands beforehand.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: À-wí-ìgbọ́, àfọ̀-ọ̀-gbọ́ tí ńfi àjèjé ọwọ́ mumi.
english_literal: He-who-will-not-listen-to-talk, he-who-will-not-listen-to-counsel, who drinks water with the bare hand.
interpretation_gold: The obstinate child drinks with the bare hand.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àwítẹ́lẹ̀ ní ńjẹ́ ọmọ́ gbẹ́nà; ọmọ kì í gbẹ́nà lásán.
english_literal: Previous-instruction enables a child to understand coded speech; a child does not naturally understand codes.
interpretation_gold: A clever child reflects the instruction he/she has received.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Awo aláwo la kì í dá lẹ́ẹ̀mejì.
english_literal: It is another person's divination that one does not repeat.
interpretation_gold: One might not put oneself out for others, but one will for oneself.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àwòdì òkè tí ńwo ìkaraun kọ̀rọ̀, kí ni yó fìgbín ṣe?
english_literal: The hawk in the sky eyes the snail-shell slyly; what will it do with a snail.
interpretation_gold: One should not waste one's time on a task one cannot master.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom

english_literal: (Employ the proper material to the task in hand.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom

english_literal: (Certain materials are of no use in some applications.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom

english_literal: The skin of the mouth cannot be used to fashion a drum.
interpretation_gold: Employ the proper materials for the task in hand.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom

english_literal: The Colobus monkey jumps to the ground; it runs for home.
interpretation_gold: When danger lurks, the wisest course is to run for safety.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom

english_literal: (They prey that knows its stalker's tricks is safe.)

english_literal: (Certain approaches one must reject as improper.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom

english_literal: Dry smoked fish is delicious, but what is one to eat before the fish is smoked?
interpretation_gold: While one must look to the future, one must also take care of the present.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ayé ńlọ, à ńtọ̀ ọ́.
english_literal: The world goes forth, and we follow.
interpretation_gold: One lives according to what life confronts one with.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom

english_literal: The world is not a thing to exchange threats with; it can inflict disaster on one.
interpretation_gold: Be wary in dealing with the world.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ayé ò ṣé-é finú hàn; bí o lọ́gbọ́n, fi síkùn ara-à rẹ.
english_literal: The world does not deserve to be trusted; if you have a store of wisdom, keep it in you.
interpretation_gold: People of the world are not reliable; whatever wisdom one wishes to pass on one should reserve for one's own use.

yoruba: Baálé àìlọ́wọ̀ ni àlejò àìlọ́wọ̀.
english_literal: An unsolicitous host makes for a visitor with no deference.
interpretation_gold: The visitor responds according to his reception.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Baálẹ̀ àgbẹ̀-ẹ́ ní òun ò ní nǹkan-án tà lọ́run, kí owó ọkà òún ṣáà ti pé.
english_literal: The chief of farmers says he has nothing to go to heaven to sell; all he cares about is fair payment for his corn.
interpretation_gold: If one does not ask for too much, one will not have to die to get it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: “Báyìí là ńṣe” níbìkan, èèwọ̀ ibòmínìn.
english_literal: “This is what we do” in one place is taboo in another.
interpretation_gold: Different people, different ways.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: If one lives with a maniac one incurs the enmity of the wise; if one shuns iyá leaves one offends the corn-gruel seller.
english_literal: (If one keeps bad company one alienates good people; if one shuns a person one shuns that person's friends.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom

english_literal: (If both sides in a dispute deserve blame, one should apportion it accordingly.)

english_literal: If one whips a child with the right hand, one embraces it with the left.
interpretation_gold: A child deserving punishment yet deserves love.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a bá jẹ̀wọ́ tán ẹ̀rín là ńrín; bí a bá yó tán orun ní ńkunni.
english_literal: After a joke one gives way to laughter; after satiation one gives way to sleep.
interpretation_gold: The action should match the occasion.

yoruba: Bí a bá kìlọ̀ fólè, ká kìlọ̀ fóníṣu ẹ̀bá ọ̀nà.
english_literal: As one warns the thief, one should also warn the owner of the wayside yams.
interpretation_gold: The offender and the tempter both deserve blame.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Compare: Bí a bá bá ẹrán wí, ká bá ẹràn wí.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom

interpretation_gold: The perceptive person can detect meaning in the slightest of signs.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a bá ńsunkún, à máa ríran.
english_literal: While one weeps, one can still see.
interpretation_gold: However accommodating one is, one should never take leave of one's good judgement.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a bá ránni níṣẹ́ ẹrú, à fi jẹ́ tọmọ.
english_literal: If one is sent on an errand like a slave, one carries it out like a freeborn.
interpretation_gold: The well-bred person removes the flaws in a message sent through him, or a task given him to perform.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a bá rántí ọjọ́ kan ìbálé, ká rántí ọjọ́ kan ìkúnlẹ̀ abiyamọ, ká rántí kan abẹ́ tí ńtani lára.
english_literal: If one remembers the day of (the loss of) virginity, one should also remember the day of a woman's delivery, and one should remember the vagina that smarts.
interpretation_gold: As one takes one's pleasures, one should be mindful of the pains that make them possible.

english_literal: When one sees a devious person one mistakes him for a good person; one talks into a basket and it leaks.
interpretation_gold: It is easy to mistake a bad person for a good person, and to place one's trust in that person.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom

english_literal: Although one has seen the morning, what about night time?
interpretation_gold: Nobody should be judged until he or she has reached the end of his or her days.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a bá sọ̀rọ̀ tán, ẹrín là ńrín; bí a bá yó tán orun ní ńkunni.
english_literal: When one is done discussing a matter one laughs, when one is satiated sleep claims one.
interpretation_gold: When a matter has been taken care of, one turns one's attention in the appropriate direction.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Compare: Bí a bá jẹ̀wọ́ tán ẹ̀rín là ńrín . . .

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a bá ṣe ohun ńlá, à fi èpè gba ara ẹni là.
english_literal: If one has committed a great offense, one frees oneself by swearing (innocence).
interpretation_gold: One's greatest duty is one's self-preservation.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a bá ta ará ilé ẹni lọ́pọ̀, a kì í rí i rà lọ́wọ̀n-ọ́n mọ́.
english_literal: If one sells a member of one's household cheap, one will not be able to buy him back at a great value.
interpretation_gold: Once one has besmirched the name of a person one is close to, one cannot later wipe it clean.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a kò bá gbé ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ sọ sínú omi gbígbóná, ká tún gbé e sọ sí tútù, kì í mọ èyí tó sàn.
english_literal: If one does not throw a toad into hot water, and then throw it into cold water, it does not know which is better.
interpretation_gold: It takes a change in circumstances to make one appreciate one's good fortune.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a kò bá gbọ́n ju àparò oko ẹni lọ, a kì í pa á.
english_literal: If one is not more clever than the partridge on one's farm, one cannot kill it.
interpretation_gold: To succeed one must be more clever than one's adversary.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a kò bá rádànán, à fòòbẹ̀ ṣẹbọ.
english_literal: If one cannot find a bat, one sacrifices a housebat.
interpretation_gold: One makes do with what one can find.
notes: See also the next entry.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a kò bá rígún a ò gbọdọ̀ ṣebọ; bí a ò bá rí àkàlà a ò gbọdọ̀ ṣorò.
english_literal: If we cannot find a vulture we may not offer a sacrifice; if we cannot find a ground hornbill we may not carry out a ritual.
interpretation_gold: Nothing can be accomplished in the absence of the requisite materials.
notes: Compare the previous entry.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a kò bá torí iṣu jẹ epo, à torí epo jẹṣu.
english_literal: If one does not eat oil because of yams, one will eat yams because of oil.
interpretation_gold: If one does not perform a duty because one likes it, one performs it because it is the right thing to do.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a kò bímọ rí, a kò ha rọ́mọ lẹ́hìn adìẹ?
english_literal: If one has never had a child, has one not seen chicks flocking after chickens?
interpretation_gold: Children are no novelty that any person does not know about.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a kò ránni sọ́jà, ọjà kì í ránni sílé.
english_literal: If one does not send a message to the market, the market does not send a message to one at home.
interpretation_gold: Unless one makes an effort, one cannot expect rewards.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a kò ṣe ọdẹ rí, a kò lè mọ ẹsẹ̀-ẹ kò-lọ-ibẹ̀un.
english_literal: If one has never hunted, one would not know the tracks of “it-did-not-go-that-way.”
interpretation_gold: One is an ignoramus in a trade that is not one's own.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí alẹ́ bá lẹ́, à fi ọmọ ayò fún ayò.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: When night comes, one gives the ayò seeds to ayò.
english_literal: (When the time comes, one puts an end to whatever one is doing.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí alẹ́ bá lẹ́, bọnnọ-bọ́nnọ́ a rẹ̀wẹ̀sì.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: When night falls, bọnnọ-bọ́nnọ́ goes limp.
english_literal: (There must be an end to every struggle and every exertion.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí alẹ́ kò lẹ́, òòbẹ̀ kì í fò.
english_literal: If night does not fall, the house bat does not fly.
interpretation_gold: All actions must await their auspicious moments.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí apá ò ká àràbà, apá lè ká egbò ìdí-i rẹ̀.
english_literal: If the arms cannot encompass the silk-cotton tree, they may encompass its root.
interpretation_gold: If one is no match for the father, one may be more than a match for the child.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí àrùn búburú bá wọ̀lú, oògùn búburú la fi ńwò ó.
english_literal: If a terrible epidemic descends on a town, it is confronted with a terrible medicine.
interpretation_gold: One matches the medicine to the disease.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí eégún ó bàá wọlẹ̀, orò ni ńṣe.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: If a masquerader wishes to disappear into the ground, it cries “Orò!”
english_literal: (A person intending to do something extraordinary should give prior warning.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí eré bí eré, àlàbọrùn-ún dẹ̀wù.
english_literal: Like play, like play, the makeshift cape became a dress.
interpretation_gold: Imperceptibly, a stop-gap arrangement has become the status quo.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ẹlẹ́rẹ̀kẹ́ régérégé bá ro ẹjọ́-ọ tirẹ̀ tán, kó rántí pé ẹlẹ́rẹ̀kẹ́ mẹ́kí á rí rò.
english_literal: After the person with smooth cheeks has stated his or her case, he or she should remember that the person with blemished cheeks will have something to say.
interpretation_gold: The person who looks good owing to the efforts of his or her subordinates should remember that they also deserve some credit.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí igí bá wó lu igi, tòkè là ńkọ́ gbé.
english_literal: If trees fall atop one another, one removes the topmost one first.
interpretation_gold: One should attend to affairs according to their urgency.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ikún bá jẹ, bí ikún bá mu, ikún a wo oòrùn alẹ́.
english_literal: When the squirrel has eaten, when the squirrel has drunk, the squirrel looks at the setting sun.
interpretation_gold: Whatever one does, one should mind the passing of time.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ilẹ̀-ẹ́ bá laná, ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ á fò gun igi.
english_literal: If the earth catches fire, the toad will hop on a tree.
interpretation_gold: If one's position becomes untenable, one seeks refuge elsewhere.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ilú bá dá sí méjì, tọba ọ̀rún là ńṣe.
english_literal: If the town is split into two, one does the will of the heavenly king.
interpretation_gold: If there is a division in one's group, one takes the side God would favor.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí iṣẹ́ kò pẹ́ ẹni, a kì í pẹ́ iṣẹ́.
english_literal: If a task does not delay one, one does not drag it out.
interpretation_gold: Tasks that are easy should be finished promptly.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí kò bá tíì rẹ ìjà, a kì í là á.
english_literal: If a fight is not yet spent, one does not intervene to end it.
interpretation_gold: One cannot end a fight that is not yet willing to end.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí kókó bá dáni, a kì í jẹ orí ìmàdò; bí a bá jẹ orí ìmàdò, a kì í lọ sí àwùjọ póńpó; bí a bá lọ sí àwùjọ póńpó, ìwọ̀n ara ẹni là ńmọ̀.
english_literal: (If one is tripped by a protruding object one should not eat a wart-hog's head; if one eats a wart-hog's head, one should not go to a gathering of cudgels; if one goes to a gathering of cudgels, one should know one's place and act accordingly.
interpretation_gold: If unforseen circumstances force one to engage in risky behavior, one should be that much more careful.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí nǹkán bá tán nílẹ̀, ọmọ ẹbọ a bọ́ síjó, àwọn tó wà níbẹ̀ a múra àti lọ.
english_literal: At the conclusion of a ceremony the acolyte commences to dance, and the onlookers prepare to make their exit.
interpretation_gold: One should not hang around after one's business is done.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí o bá já ng ó so ọ́, kókó yó wà láàárín-in rẹ̀.
english_literal: “If you break I will retie you”; there will be a knot in it.
interpretation_gold: Something repaired is seldom the same as something unspoilt.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí o kò gbọ́ Ègùn, o kò gbọ́ wọ̀yọ̀-wọ̀yọ̀?

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: If you do not understand Ègùn, do you not recognize signs that someone is speaking?
english_literal: (One may not understand what a person says, but one will be able to tell that the person is speaking.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí o máa ṣe aya Olúgbọ́n ṣe aya Olúgbọ́n; bí o máa ṣe aya Arẹsà ṣe aya Arẹsà, kí o yéé pákọ̀kọ̀ lẹ́gbẹ̀ẹ́ ògiri; ẹni tí yó ṣe aya Olúfẹ̀ a kógbá wálé.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: If you will be a wife to the Olúgbọ́n be a wife to him; if you will be a wife to the Arẹsà be a wife to him, and stop sneaking around hugging walls; a person who would be the wife of the Olúfẹ̀ must gather her affairs into the house.
english_literal: (Once one has chosen a course, one should commit oneself completely to it.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí obìnrin ò bá gbé ilé tó méjì, kì í mọ èyí tó sàn.
english_literal: If a woman has not lived in at least two homes, she never knows which is better.
interpretation_gold: Unless one has tasted some adversity, one does not appreciate one's good fortune.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ojú bá mọ́, olówò a gbówò; ọ̀rànwú a gbé kẹ́kẹ́; ajagun a gbé apata; àgbẹ̀ a jí tòun tòrúkọ́; ọmọ ọdẹ a jí tapó tọrán; ajíwẹṣẹ a bá odò omi lọ.
english_literal: When day breaks, the trader takes up his trade; the cotton spinner picks up the spindle; the warrior grabs his shield; the farmer gets up with his hoe; the son of the hunter arises with his quiver and his bows; he-who-wakes-and-washes-with-soap makes his way to the river.
interpretation_gold: When morning comes, everybody should embark on something useful.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ojú bá rí ọ̀rọ̀, a wò ó fín.
english_literal: When the eyes come upon a matter, they must look hard and well.
interpretation_gold: Imperfect understanding of a matter causes difficulties.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ojú ọmọdé ò tó ìtàn, a bá àwígbọ́.
english_literal: If a youth's eyes do not witness a story, they should be good for hearsay.
interpretation_gold: If one does not witness something, one learns from those who did.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí olósùn-ún bá lọ osùn, ara-a rẹ̀ ní ńfi dánwò.
english_literal: When the camwood powder seller grinds the powder, she tests it on her own body.
interpretation_gold: One tries one's remedy on one's self before offering it to others.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí òrìṣá bá mú ẹlẹ́hìn, kí abuké máa múra sílẹ̀.
english_literal: If the gods take a person with a protruding back, the humpback should make ready.
interpretation_gold: If a person like one suffers a certain fate, one is at risk.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí òwe bí òwe là ńlùlù ògìdìgbó; olọgbọ́n ní ńjó o; ọ̀mọ̀ràn ní ńsìí mọ̀ọ́.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Like proverbs, like proverbs one plays the ògìdìgbó music;
interpretation_gold: Only the wise can follow subtle discourses.
notes: only the wise can dance to it, and only the knowledgeable know it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí òwe bí òwe nIfá ńsọ̀rọ̀.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Like proverbs, like proverbs are the pronouncements of Ifá.
interpretation_gold: The most profound speech is indirect and subtle.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ọ̀bùn ò mọ èrè, a mọ ojú owó.
english_literal: If the filthy person does not know profit, he should know his capital.
interpretation_gold: If a person cannot improve a matter, he should not worsen it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ọkùnrín réjò, tóbìrín pa á, à ní kéjò má ṣáà lọ.
english_literal: If a man sees a snake, and a woman kills it, what matters is that the snake does not escape.
interpretation_gold: One should not be a stickler about roles.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí Ọlọ́run-ún bá ti fọ̀tá ẹni hanni, kò lè pani mọ́.
english_literal: Once God has revealed one's enemy to one, he can no longer kill one.
interpretation_gold: Knowledge neutralizes dangers.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ọlọgbọ́n bá ńfi wèrè se iṣu, ọ̀mọ̀ràn a máa fi gègé yàn án.
english_literal: If a wise person is cooking yams in an insane way, a knowing person picks them with stakes.
interpretation_gold: If a person tries to mislead one, one finds one's own direction.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ọmọ́ bá jágbọ́n-ọn kíké, ìyá-a rẹ̀ a jágbọ́n-ọn rírẹ̀ ẹ́.
english_literal: If a child learns the trick of crying, the mother learns the trick of consoling him or her.
interpretation_gold: One must be ready to adapt to cope with any situation.
notes: See the next entry also.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ọmọ́ bá jágbọ́n-ọn kíkú, ìyá ẹ̀ a jágbọ́n-ọn sísin.
english_literal: If a child learns the trick of dying, his mother should learn the trick of burying.
interpretation_gold: One should learn to meet wiles with wiles.
notes: See also the preceding entry.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ọmọ́ bá yó, a fikùn han baba.
english_literal: When a child is full, he shows his stomach to his father.
interpretation_gold: When one accomplishes one's goals, one feels like celebrating; also, one should show one's appreciation to one's benefactor.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ọmọdé bá dúpẹ́ ore àná, a rí tòní gbà.
english_literal: If a child expresses gratitude for yesterday's favor, he will receive today's.
interpretation_gold: The grateful person encourages others to do him more favors.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ọmọdé bá ḿbẹ́ igi, àgbàlagbà a máa wo ibi tí yó wòó sí.
english_literal: If a youth is felling a tree, an elder will be considering where it will fall.
interpretation_gold: Unlike the youth, the elder is mindful of consequences.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ọmọdé bá mọ ayò, ẹyọ la ó fi pa á.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: If a child is an adept ayò player, one defeats him with single seeds.
english_literal: (A precocious child may be almost as accomplished as an adult, but will not be quite as accomplished.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ọmọdé bá ṣubú a wo iwájú; bí àgbá bá ṣubú a wo ẹ̀hìn.
english_literal: When a youth falls he looks ahead; when an elder falls he looks behind.
interpretation_gold: The youth is mindful of what his superiors think of him, while the elder is mindful of what the young think of him.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Compare: Bí ọmọdé bá máa só a wo iwájú . . .

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ọmọdé ò bá rí oko baba ẹlòmíràn, a ní kò sí oko baba ẹni tó tó ti baba òun.
english_literal: If a youth has never seen another person's father's farm, he says no body's father's farm is as large as his father's.
interpretation_gold: Until one has seen other people's great accomplishments, one is overly impressed by one's own.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ọmọdé kọ iyán àná, ìtàn la ó pa fún un.
english_literal: If a child refuses yesterday's pounded yams, it is stories one treats the child to.
interpretation_gold: A person who boycotts a meal or some entitlement simply deprives him/herself of some benefits.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ọ̀rán bá pẹ́ nílẹ̀, gbígbọ́n ní ńgbọ́n.
english_literal: If a problem remains long enough, it becomes clever.
interpretation_gold: If one keeps at it long enough, one will find the solution for any problem.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ọwọ́ ò bá ṣeé ṣán, à ká a lérí.
english_literal: If the arms cannot be swung, one carries them on one's head.
interpretation_gold: If one cannot do as one would, one does what one can.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí sòbìyà yó bàá degbò, olúgambe là á wí fún.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: If guinea worm is becoming an ulcer, one should inform olúgambe.
english_literal: (When a problem arises, one must consult those who can solve it.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí túlàsí bá di méjì, ọ̀kan là ḿmú.
english_literal: When emergencies number two, one concentrates on one.
interpretation_gold: One concentrates on one problem at a time.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: “Bùn mi níṣu kan” kì í ṣáájú “Ẹkú oko òo.”
english_literal: “Give me one yam” does not precede “Greetings to you on the farm.”
interpretation_gold: One does not ask a favor of, or transact any business with any person without first exchanging pleasantries with the person.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Compare “Ṣe mí níṣu” ní ńṣíwájú “ẹ kúuṣẹ́” bí?

english_literal: [Back to text]

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: 49. Ayò  is the game played with seeds in a board with twelve scooped holes, a game popular in many parts of the continent.
english_literal: [Back to text]

english_literal: [Back to text]
notes: 51. The persons named are titled people, whose wives would be expected to be above reproach. [Back to text]

english_literal: [Back to text]

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Dà-á-sílẹ̀-ká-tun-pín, ogún ijọ́un, a ò pín in re.
english_literal: The recent throw-it-all-on-the-floor-that-we-may-redistribute-it inheritance was not well distributed the first time around.
interpretation_gold: Whatever needs to be done again must not have been done well the first time.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Dídì ní ḿmú abẹ mú.
english_literal: It is wrapping that makes a knife sharp.
interpretation_gold: Only by taking great care of them does one keep one's possessions in good shape.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Díẹ̀-díẹ̀ nimú ẹlẹ́dẹ̀ẹ́ fi ńwọgbà.
english_literal: It is bit by bit that the nose of the pig enters the fence.
interpretation_gold: A small problem, if not attended to, becomes unmanageable.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: DÍfá-dÍfá ò fIfá ṣeré.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: The diviner does not take Ifá lightly.
english_literal: (One should not be careless about one's livelihood.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Dùgbẹ̀-dùgbẹ̀ kì í fi ẹyin rẹ̀ sílẹ̀.
english_literal: The egg-bearing spider never leaves its eggs behind.
interpretation_gold: One does not turn one's back on one's treasure.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Dúró o kíkà; bí o ò dúró kíkà, ìkà a ba tìrẹ jẹ́.
english_literal: Stop and say hello to the wicked; if you do not say hello to the wicked, the wicked will find problems for you.
interpretation_gold: One's best defence against the wicked is ingratiation.
notes: . Previous Contents Next

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ebi ńpa mí ọlọ́ṣẹ ńkiri; ìgbà tí ng ò wẹnú ng ó ṣe wẹ̀de?
english_literal: I am hungry and the soap seller hawks her wares; when I have not washed my inside, how can I wash my outside?
interpretation_gold: One must order one's priorities sensibly.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ebi ò pàJèṣà ó lóun ò jẹ̀kọ Ọ̀yọ́; ebí pa ọmọ Obòkun ó jẹ ori.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: The Ijeṣa person is not hungry and he rejects corn-loaf prepared by an Ọ̀yọ́ person; when hunger gripped the son of Obokun (an apellation for Ijeṣa people) he ate ori(the Ọ̀yọ́ name for corn-loaf.)
english_literal: (It is when one is not desperate that one is choosy.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ebi ò pàmọ̀le ó ní òun ò jẹ àáyá; ebí pa Súlè ó jọ̀bọ.
english_literal: The muslim is not hungry and he vows he will not eat a red Colobus monkey; hunger gripped Suleiman and he ate a monkey.
interpretation_gold: A desperate person is seldom finicky.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Eégún Ẹ̀gbá, Ẹ̀gbá ní ńfọ̀.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: The Ẹ̀gbá masquerader must needs speak Ẹ̀gbá.
interpretation_gold: One should speak to others in a manner that befits one, and that will facilitate one's business with them.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Eégún tí yó gbeni là ńdáṣọ fún; òrìṣà tí yó gbeni là ńsìn; bi igí bá gbè mí mà kó obì mà bọ igi.
english_literal: It is the masquerader that succors one that one makes shrouds for; it is the god that succors one that one worships; if a tree succors me, I will take kolanuts and worship the tree.
interpretation_gold: One should confine one's efforts to profitable ventures, and one's service to appreciative people.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Eégún tí yó ṣe bíi Lébé, Lébé ni yó dà; èyí tí yó tàkìtì bí Olúfolé, òfurugbàdà ni yó ta á.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: The masquerader that will perform like Lébé must become like Lébé; the one that will sumersault like Olúfolé (meaning “Great-One-Jumps-A-House”) must perform his feat in the open spaces.
english_literal: (One must prepare oneself and gather one's resources before one attempts momentous tasks.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ejò-ó rí ihò tó há ó kó wọ̀ ọ́; ìyá-a rẹ̀-ẹ́ lọ́wọ́ àti fà á yọ?
english_literal: A snake sees a tight hole and crawls into it; has its mother hands to pull it out?
interpretation_gold: One had better be certain that one would be able to extricate oneself before one ventures into tight spots.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Elékuru kì í kiri lóko.
english_literal: The seller of steamed ground beans does not hawk her wares on a farm.
interpretation_gold: One wastes one's time attempting to sell things to those who produce them.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Èló là ńra adìẹ òkókó, tí à ńgba ọmọ-ọ rẹ̀ sìn?
english_literal: How much does a hen cost that one would contract to raise chicks for the owner?
interpretation_gold: Certain obligations are not worth the trouble.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Èmi-ò-níí-fẹ́-obìnrin-tẹ́nìkan-ńfẹ́, olúwarẹ̀ ò níí fẹ́ obìnrin ni.
english_literal: I-will-court-no-woman-being-courted-by-another-man will court no woman at all.
interpretation_gold: A person who wants exclusive rights to a woman (or anything) will look for a long time and in vain.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Èmi-ò-níí-ṣu-imí-le-imí, olúwarẹ̀ ó rìn jìnnà ààtàn.
english_literal: I-will-not-defecate-on-existing-excrement will walk a good distance into the bush.
interpretation_gold: People who are too finicky will pay in effort and delay for their habits.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Èpè la fi ńwo èpè sàn.
english_literal: Curses are the antidote for curses.
interpretation_gold: One matches the remedy to the affliction.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Epo ló ṣeé jẹṣu; àkàsọ̀ ló ṣeé gun àká; obìnrín dùn-ún bá sùn ju ọkùnrin lọ.
english_literal: It is palm oil that goes best with yams; it is a ladder that is best for climbing granaries; a woman is more pleasant to make love to than a man.
interpretation_gold: Certain things are fit for certain purposes; not anything will do anytime.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Epo lojú ọbẹ̀.
english_literal: Palm-oil is the countenance of stew.
interpretation_gold: One should be particularly attentive to that one ingredient or thing whose absence mars the entire project.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Eré là ńfọmọ ayò ṣe.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: All one does with ayò seeds is play.
english_literal: (One should take time for pleasure when one may.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Èrò kì í mọ ibùsọ̀ kọ́rùn ó wọ̀ ọ́.
english_literal: A wayfarer does not know the location of the rest stop and yet have his neck crushed from the weight of a heavy load.
interpretation_gold: One measures one's exertions to suit one's capacity.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ète lẹ̀gbọ́n; ìmọ̀ràn làbúrò; bí-a-ó-ti-ṣe lẹ̀kẹta wọn.
english_literal: Intention is the eldest, contemplation is the next, and plan of action is the third.
interpretation_gold: First there is the goal, next a contemplation of it, and finally a plan for attaining it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ètò lòfin kìn-ín-ní lóde ọ̀run.
english_literal: Order is the first law in heaven.
interpretation_gold: Whatever one does, one must be orderly.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ewúrẹ́ ò ṣe-e fiṣu ṣọ́.
english_literal: A goat is not a wise choice as the guard over yams.
interpretation_gold: Do not entrust your affairs to your enemy.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Èyí tó yẹ ará iwájú, èrò ẹ̀hìn fiyè sílẹ̀.
english_literal: (To) what turned out favorably for those going ahead, you coming behind, pay close attention.
interpretation_gold: Learn from the examples of others.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: 55. This is another designation for the people of Abẹ́òkúta and their language.
english_literal: [Back to text]

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: 56. An alárìnjó (itinerant dancer) type.
english_literal: [Back to text]
notes: 57. People sometimes would agree to raise domestic animals for other people in the hope of sharing in their litter. [Back to text] 58. The proverb obviously speaks from a man's point of view. [Back to text] 59. The Yoruba believe that the more palm-oil goes into a stew the better the stew. [Back to text] . Previous Contents Next

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹ̀bẹ̀ là ḿbẹ òṣìkà pé kó tún ìlú-u rẹ̀ ṣe.
english_literal: One can only remonstrate with a wicked person to urge him or her to improve his or her town.
interpretation_gold: Gentle pleas are the only likely means of getting contrary people to do what is right.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹbọ díẹ̀, oògùn díẹ̀, ní ńgba aláìkú là.
english_literal: A little sacrifice, a little medicine, is what keeps the one who does not die alive.
interpretation_gold: One should not place all of one's faith in a single solution to a problem.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹbọ ẹnìkan là ńfi ẹnìkan rú.
english_literal: It is a sacrifice on behalf of only one person that demands only one person as offering.
interpretation_gold: Extraordinary problems demand extraordinary solutions.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹ̀fẹ̀-ẹ́ dẹ̀fẹ̀ iyán; a paláwẹ́ ẹ̀kọ baálé ilé ní ẹ̀ ńpèun bí?
english_literal: The teasing involves pounded yams; the corn-loaf is unwrapped, and the father of the household asks, “Did someone call me?”
interpretation_gold: A person who wants something badly will not let a little teasing put him or her off taking it.
notes: See the next entry also.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹ̀fẹ̀-ẹ́ dẹ̀fẹ̀ iyán; ò báà gbémi lulẹ̀ ng ó bàá ọ jẹun.
english_literal: The teasing involves pounded yam; even if you throw me on the ground I will eat with you.
interpretation_gold: No amount of teasing will stop me from doing what I have in mind.
notes: Compare the preceding entry.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹgbẹ́ ẹni kì í wọ́n láyé ká wá a lọ sọ́run.
english_literal: One does not upon failing to find suitable company in this world go looking in heaven.
interpretation_gold: If one cannot find what one wants, one should learn to do without it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹjọ́ a-fẹ́ni-lóbìnrin là ńwí; a kì í wíjọ́ a-fẹ́ni-lọ́mọ.
english_literal: One may complain about a person who courts one's wife, but one does not complain about a person who courts one's daughter.
interpretation_gold: One should not pursue causes without good grounds.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹ̀ẹ̀kan lejò ńyánni.
english_literal: One gets bitten by a snake only once.
interpretation_gold: The same disaster does not befall one more than once; after the first time one learns to avoid it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹlẹ́nu-ú tóó rí sá.
english_literal: An overly loquacious person is someone to flee from.
interpretation_gold: Be wary of loquacious people.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹlẹ́dẹ̀ẹ́ ní ọjọ́ tí òún ti jágbọ́n-ọn hùn, ọjọ́ náà ni ọ̀rọ̀ ò ti nìun lára mọ́.
english_literal: The pig says since the day it learned to reply to every statement with a grunt it has not got into any trouble.
interpretation_gold: A person who says nothing seldom gets in trouble.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: This is a variant of Àjàpá ní ọjọ́ tí òún ti jágbọ́nọn òo . . . and Ẹrùu òo kì í wọni lọ́rùn.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹlẹ́jọ́ ṣa èyí tó wù ú wí.
english_literal: The person with complaints selects the most pressing ones to press.
interpretation_gold: One should concentrate on one's most pressing problems.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni a óò gbé òkú-u rẹ̀ sin, a kì í sọ pé ó ńrùn pani.
english_literal: One does not complain that a corpse one will have to bury stinks.
interpretation_gold: One should not run down a person or thing that will eventually devolve to one's care.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni a pé kó wáá wo kọ̀bì: ó ní kí nìyí kọ́bi-kọ̀bi?
english_literal: The person invited to take a look at the palace stateroom: he exclaims, “What a maze of apartments!”
interpretation_gold: One should not waste one's breath expressing the obvious.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni à ńwò kì í wòran.
english_literal: The person people have gathered to watch should not himself or herself be a spectator.
interpretation_gold: One should not ignore one's problems to dwell on others'.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni a wí fún ko gbọ́; ẹni a fọ̀ fún kó gbà; èyí tí ò gbọ́ yó filẹ̀ bora.
english_literal: Whoever people speak to should listen; whoever people instruct should accept instruction; the one who does not listen will be covered by the earth.
interpretation_gold: Refusal to heed advice can be deadly.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni àìgbọ́n pa ló pọ̀; ẹni ọgbọ́n pa ò tó ǹkan.
english_literal: People killed by folly are innumerable; people killed by wisdom are few.
interpretation_gold: Few things kill more surely than folly.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹní bá ríkun nímú ọlọ́jà ní ńfọn ọ́n.
english_literal: Whoever sees mucus in the nose of the king is the one who cleans it.
interpretation_gold: Tactless or indiscreet people usually rue their bad judgement.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Compare Ẹni tí ó bá sọ pé ẹsè eeégún ńhàn . . .

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹní bá tó ẹni-í gbà là ńké pè.
english_literal: One appeals only to those capable of helping one.
interpretation_gold: One should not seek the aid of feckless people.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹní du ara-a rẹ̀ lóyè Apènà: kó tó jẹ ẹran ọ̀fẹ́, ó dọ̀run.
english_literal: Whoever deprives himself of the title of Apena will wait until he dies before tasting free meat.
interpretation_gold: If one does not grab opportunities when they present themselves, one is in for a difficult life.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹní gbọ́n juni lọ ní ńtẹni nÍfá.
english_literal: It is someone wiser than one who consults the oracle for one.
interpretation_gold: One receives advice only from those qualified to offer it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹní léku méjì á pòfo.
english_literal: Whoever chases after two rats will catch neither.
interpretation_gold: If one pursues two or more objectives at once one is liable to achieve neither.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹní máa ké ìbòsí á pa baba rẹ̀ jẹ.
english_literal: Whoever wishes to raise an alarm will have to murder his father.
interpretation_gold: Whoever acts without cause will have to justify his action by manufacturing some cause.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹní rúbọ òrìṣà-á gbọ́dọ̀ rú ti èèyàn kí ẹbọ-ọ́ tó gbà.
english_literal: Whoever offers a sacrifice to a deity must also offer a sacrifice to humans in order for the sacrifice to be efficacious.
interpretation_gold: One can please the gods and yet run afoul of humans.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tí a bá fi orí-i rẹ̀ fọ́ àgbọn ò níí jẹ níbẹ̀.
english_literal: The person on whose head a coconut is broken will not share in eating it.
interpretation_gold: Whoever takes foolhardy risks in pursuit of an end seldom lives to enjoy it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tí a bá ḿbá nájà là ńwò, a kì í wo ariwo ọjà.
english_literal: One pays attention to the person with whom one is bargaining, not to the commotion of the market place.
interpretation_gold: One should keep one's mind on one's business and leave extraneous matters aside.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tí a wífún kó gbọ́; ẹni tí kò gbọ́, tara-a rẹ̀ ni yó dà.
english_literal: Let the person one advises heed one; the heedless person places himself at risk.
interpretation_gold: Those who refuse instruction lay the foundation for their own ruin.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tí ẹ̀gún gún lẹ́sẹ̀ ní ńṣe lákáǹláká tẹ̀lé alábẹ́rẹ́.
english_literal: It is the person with a thorn in his foot who limps to the person with a needle.
interpretation_gold: The person in need of help should make some effort in his own behalf, and not expect his helper to make all the necessary effort.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tí kò gbọ́n lààwẹ̀ ńgbò.
english_literal: Only the unwise hungers while fasting.
interpretation_gold: The resourceful person can find a way around any difficulty.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tí kò mọ iṣẹ́-ẹ́ jẹ́ ní ńpààrà lẹ́ẹ̀mejì.
english_literal: It is a person who does not know how to carry out instructions that is forced to repeat his or her efforts.
interpretation_gold: One saves time and effort by doing things right the first time.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tí kò mọ ọba ní ńfọba ṣeré.
english_literal: Only a person who does not know the king trifles with the king.
interpretation_gold: The wise person recognizes potential danger and avoids it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tí ó lè jà ni yóò kúnlẹ̀ kalẹ́.
english_literal: It is the incorrigible fighter who has to remain on his or her knees until nightfall.
interpretation_gold: The person who cannot stay out of a fight will spend his or her time incessantly stating cases.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tí yó bọ Ògún, yó ra ọjà-a tirẹ̀ lọ́tọ̀.
english_literal: The person who will worship Ògun will keep his or her market purchases separate from those of others.
interpretation_gold: If one's priorities are incompatible with those of others, one parts company with them.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tí yó fò yó bẹ̀rẹ̀.
english_literal: The person who will leap must first crouch.
interpretation_gold: One must make adequate preparations for any project.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tí yó mu ẹ̀kọ fòrò, yó bàá ọmọ ẹlẹ́kọ ṣeré.
english_literal: Whoever wishes to eat steaming corn pap will play with the child of the seller.
interpretation_gold: One must ingratiate oneself with the person from whom one expects a favor.
notes: This is a variant of the next entry.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tí yó mu ẹ̀kọ ọ̀fẹ́ yó bàá ọmọ ẹlẹ́kọ ṣeré.
english_literal: The person who wishes to eat free corn pap will play with the seller's child.
interpretation_gold: Nothing comes free.
notes: Compare the preceding entry.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tí yó ṣòwò àlè, ẹní-i rẹ̀ ní ńká; ẹni tí yó ṣòwò-o Ṣàngó, ààjà-a rẹ̀ ní ńrà.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Whoever chooses concubinage as a practice must provide herself with a sleeping mat; whoever chooses Ṣàngò's trade (one to do with metal) must purchase his magical rattle.
english_literal: (One prepares oneself according to what is proper for one's chosen trade.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tí yó yàáni lówó, tí kò níí sinni, ohùn ẹnu-u rẹ̀ la ti ḿmọ̀.
english_literal: The person who will lend one money and will not keep pestering one for repayment: one can tell from the tone of his or her voice.
interpretation_gold: The way people talk is a good indication of their character.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó bá da omi síwájú á tẹ ilẹ̀ tútù.
english_literal: Whoever throws water ahead will step on cool earth.
interpretation_gold: The future will look kindly on those who look well to the future.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó bá fi ojù àná wòkú, ẹbọra a bọ́ ọ láṣọ.
english_literal: Whoever looks at the dead with yesterday's eyes will be stripped naked by the spirits.
interpretation_gold: One behaves towards people according to the heights they have attained, not according to the way they used to be.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó bá máa jẹ ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ a jẹ èyí tó lẹ́yin.
english_literal: If one must eat a toad one should eat one with eggs.
interpretation_gold: If one must suffer, one might as well do so with panache.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó bá máa lu òṣùgbó a lu ńlá; kékeré ẹgbẹ̀fà, ńlá ẹgbẹ̀fà.
english_literal: Whoever will smite a secret-cult priest had better smite an important one; for a lowly one twelve hundred cowries in fines, and for an important one twelve hundred cowries.
interpretation_gold: If the penalty for a small offence is the same as that for a grievous one, one might as well throw all caution to the wind.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó bá máa mú ọ̀bọ a ṣe bí ọ̀bọ.
english_literal: Whoever wishes to catch a monkey must act like a monkey.
interpretation_gold: To succeed against an adversary, or with a person one desires, one must suit one's approach to the other's ways.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó bá mọ ìdí ọ̀ràn tẹ́lẹ̀ ní ḿbu àbùjá èké.
english_literal: It is a person who has prior knowledge of the facts of a matter that can foil a devious person's attempts to skirt them.
interpretation_gold: Prior knowledge is the surest weapon against lies.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó bá ní igbà-á lò, bí igbà-á bá já, kó dúró so ó.
english_literal: If one must use a tree-climbing rope and it breaks, one must pause to repair it.
interpretation_gold: One must make the time to attend to chores that must be performed.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó bá pẹ́ lórí imí, eṣinṣin kéṣinṣin yó ò bá a níbẹ̀.
english_literal: Whoever prolongs his or her defecating will be visited by a host of flies.
interpretation_gold: Nothing good comes of dawdling over what one must do.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó bá rántí Efuji, kó má fi ore ṣe ẹṣin.
english_literal: Whoever remembers Efuji should show no kindness to any horse.
interpretation_gold: One should remember those who have caused one injury, and remember to show them no favor.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó bá rántí ọjọ́ ní ńṣe ọmọ òkú pẹ̀lẹ́; ta ní jẹ́ ṣe ọmọ eégún lóore?
english_literal: Those who gratefully remember past favors extend compassion to the survivors of the deceased; who would rather show compassion to the child of a masquerader?
interpretation_gold: When a good person dies, his or her survivors inherit the good will of those who remember him or her well.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó bá sọ pé ẹsẹ̀ eégún ńhàn ní ńwá abẹ́rẹ́ lọ.
english_literal: Whoever announces that the legs of the masquerader are showing is the one who goes in search of a needle.
interpretation_gold: Some sights the eyes must not acknowledge seeing.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Compare Bí ojú bá rí, ẹnu a dákẹ́and Ẹní bá ríkun nímú ọba...

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó bá yá ìwọ̀fà ẹgbàá, tòun tirẹ̀ ní ńlọ ata kúnná.
english_literal: Whoever hires a pawn for only sixpence will join the pawn in grinding pepper.
interpretation_gold: Whatever comes too cheaply is sure to work unsatisfactorily.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Compare Ẹni tó fẹ́ni ní àfẹ́ìlówó . . . below.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó dùbúlẹ̀-ẹ́ ṣe oògùn ìjàkadì tán.
english_literal: The person who remains prone has perfected the charm for wrestling.
interpretation_gold: The wise person forestalls problems.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó fi irun dúdú ṣeré, yó fi funfun sin ẹniẹlẹ́ni.
english_literal: Whoever plays around with his or her black hair will serve others with his or her white hair.
interpretation_gold: If one wastes one's youth, one spends one's old age struggling for a living.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó fi owó-o rẹ̀ ra ẹṣin, kò níí jẹ́ kó ṣe àrìnjẹ́.
english_literal: Whoever paid his or her own money for a horse will not let it be sacrificed for a good-luck charm.
interpretation_gold: One guards one's treasures jealously.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó gbajúmọ̀ tí kò mọ èèyàn-án kí, òun òbúrẹ́wà ẹgbẹ́ra.
english_literal: The dandy who does not know how to extend greetings to people is no different from a boor.
interpretation_gold: Good looks without the social graces amount to nothing.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó máa tẹ́ òkú ọ̀pọ̀lọ́, yó nìí ilé ògbóni tirẹ̀ lọ́tọ̀.
english_literal: Whoever wishes to lay a dead toad in state will have to build his own cult shrine separately.
interpretation_gold: Whoever wishes to do the absurd should not expect the cooperation or approval of others.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó máa yáni lẹ́wù, ti ọrùn-un rẹ̀ là ńwò.
english_literal: If a person offers to lend one a dress, one should consider what he or she has on.
interpretation_gold: One should be discriminating about those from whom one will accept favors.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó mi kùkùté, araa rẹ̀ ní ńmì.
english_literal: The person who shakes a tree stump shakes himself.
interpretation_gold: Whoever takes on an invincible adversary fashions his or her own defeat.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó mọ ẹtu ní ńkì í ní “òbèjé, ẹlẹ́sẹ̀ ọwọ̀.”
english_literal: It is someone who knows the duiker intimately who can recite its praise, “spindle-legged duiker.”
interpretation_gold: Only those deeply involved in a profession are versed in its jargon.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó ńṣápẹ́ fún wèrè jó, òun àti wèrè ọ̀kan-ùn.
english_literal: The person who claps for a mad person to dance to is no different from the mad person.
interpretation_gold: Whoever joins the imbecile in his or her games is himself or herself an imbecile.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó pa kẹ́tẹ́kẹ́tẹ́ yó ru káyá ẹrù.
english_literal: The person who kills the donkey will carry a heavy burden.
interpretation_gold: Whoever is careless with his/her resources will pay dearly in the future.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó ránṣẹ́ sí orò-ó bẹ̀wẹ̀ fún àìsùn.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Whoever sends for Orò is contracting for sleeplessness.
english_literal: (Whoever deliberately provokes trouble should be prepared for a difficult time.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó re Ìbàdán tí kò dé ilé Olúyọ̀lé, oko igi ló lọ.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Whoever goes to Ibadan and does not visit Oluyọle's house merely went wood gathering.
english_literal: (Whoever misses the principal sight of any place might as well not have visited the place at all.).

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó rúbọ tí kò gba èèwọ̀, bí ẹni tó fi owó ẹbọ ṣòfò ni.
english_literal: The person who makes a sacrifice but does not follow the prescribed taboos is just like someone who throws away the money for the sacrifice.
interpretation_gold: A person who knows of the remedy but does not apply it is as badly off as the person who does not know the remedy at all.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó sọ ẹlẹ́dẹ̀ lékùrọ́, oúnjẹ ló fún un.
english_literal: The person who throws palm-nuts at a pig gives food to it.
notes: (One does not douse a fire by throwing oil on it).

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹni tó torí òtútù fi ọmọrí odó yáná ò gbọdọ̀ retí a-ti-jẹyán.
english_literal: Whoever because of cold weather uses the pestle as kindling to warm him/herself must not expect to eat pounded yams.
interpretation_gold: One should not jeopardize one's long-term interests by indulging in immediate gratifications.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹnu àìmẹ́nu, ètè àìmétè, ní ḿmú ọ̀ràn bá ẹ̀rẹ̀kẹ́.
english_literal: A mouth that will not stay shut, lips that will not stay closed, are what bring trouble to the cheeks.
interpretation_gold: The words that the mouth and lips allow to escape usually bring the slap to the cheek; a person who cannot keep his/her mouth shut often lands in trouble.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹnu ehoro ò gba ìjánu.
english_literal: A rabbit's mouth does not accept a leash.
interpretation_gold: Do not adopt an inappropriate remedy for a problem.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹ̀rẹ̀kẹ́ ni ilé ẹ̀rín.
english_literal: The cheeks are the home of laughter.
interpretation_gold: Suit the means to the project.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹ̀rù bíbà ní ḿmúni pe àjẹ́ ní ará ire.
english_literal: It is fear that makes one call witches the good people.
interpretation_gold: It is wise to curry the favor of fearful or malicious people.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹrù-u hòo kì í wọni lọ́rùn.
english_literal: “I agree” is not a load that causes one's neck to shrink.
notes: (Saying one agrees, even when one does not, spares one a great deal of headache.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Compare Àjàpá ní ọjọ́ tí òún ti jágbọ́n-ọn . . .

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹ̀sín alátọ̀sí ò sí lọ́wọ́ òkóbó.
english_literal: The ridiculing of the person with gonorrhea does not belong with the eunuch.
interpretation_gold: Do not ridicule a person whose condition is no worse than yours'.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹyẹ igbó kì í mọ fífò ọ̀dàn.
english_literal: The bird of the forest does not know how to fly in the grassland.
interpretation_gold: When one is in a strange environment, one becomes a dunce.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ẹyẹ ńwá àtifò, wọ́ ńsọ òkò sí i.
english_literal: A bird is preparing for flight, and people throw stones at it.
interpretation_gold: One needs little encouragement to do what one is determined to do anyway; being forced to do what one wishes to do anyway is no punishment.
