part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀bẹ ńwólé ara ẹ̀ ó ní òún ḿba àkọ̀ jẹ́.
english_literal: The knife is destroying its own home, it says it is ruining the sheath.
interpretation_gold: Said of people whose actions will hurt them more than they will hurt other people.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: This is a variant of Idà ńwólé ara-a ẹ̀ . . .

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọbẹ̀ tí baálé kì í jẹ, ìyálé ilé kì í sè é.
english_literal: The sort of stew the man of the house will not eat, the woman of the house should not cook.
interpretation_gold: One should not do what one knows one's comrades hate.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀dẹ̀ ọmọ ńfi ìdò ṣeré.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: An idiot child that plays with ìdò flowers.
english_literal: (A simpleton does not know the value of anything.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀dẹ̀dẹ̀ ò gba òró, àfi abẹ́ ọdán.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: The porch does not accommodate standing people; only the shade of the (ọdán) banyan tree does.
english_literal: (An invitation to repair to another place outside other people's earshot to discuss confidential matters.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀fàfà fohùn ṣakin.
english_literal: The tree-bear wins renown with its voice.
interpretation_gold: The loud person wins attention.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọgbọ́n a-dákọ-kéré ò tó ti a-yọwó-má-rà.
english_literal: The cunning of the person who skimps on the measure of her corn meal is not as great as that of the would-be purchaser who refuses to buy.
interpretation_gold: One does not have to patronize a dishonest trader.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọgbọ́n dùn-ún gbọ́n; ìmọ́ dùn-ún mọ̀.
english_literal: Wisdom is a good thing to have; knowledge is a good thing to have.
interpretation_gold: Always seek wisdom and knowledge.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọgbọ́n ju agbára.
english_literal: Wisdom is greater than strength.
interpretation_gold: Always prefer wisdom to strength.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọgbọ́n kì í tán.
english_literal: Wisdom is never used up.
interpretation_gold: There will always be a place and some use for wisdom.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọgbọn la fi ńgbé ayé.
english_literal: One needs wisdom to live in this world.
interpretation_gold: Wisdom is indispensable.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọgbọ́n lajá fi ńpa ìkokò bọ Ifá.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: It is cunning that the dog employs in order to sacrifice a wolf to Ifá.
english_literal: (A cunning person can get the better of people far more powerful than he.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọgbọ́n ní ńṣẹgun; ìmọ̀ràn ní ńṣẹ́ ẹ̀tẹ̀.
english_literal: Cunning wins battles; knowledge defeats plots.
interpretation_gold: Cunning and knowledge will help one prevail.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọgbọ́n ọlọgbọ́n la fi ńṣọgbọ́n, ìmọ̀ràn ẹnìkan ò tọ́ bọ̀rọ̀.
english_literal: One learns wisdom from other people's wisdom one person's knowledge does not amount to anything.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọgbọ́n ọlọgbọ́n ò jẹ́ ká pe àgbà ní wèrè.
english_literal: Other people's wisdom saves the elder from being called a lunatic.
interpretation_gold: The person who can learn from others will avoid a lot of embarrassment.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọgbọ́n tí ahún gbọ́n, ẹ̀hìn ni yó máa tọ ti ìgbín.
english_literal: The cunning that the tortoise has will always rank behind that of the snail.
interpretation_gold: Some people cannot hope to be more cunning than some others.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọgbọ́n tí ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ fi pa ẹfọ̀n ló fi ńjẹ ẹ́.
english_literal: The same cunning with which the toad killed the buffalo will show it how to eat the prey.
interpretation_gold: If a person has proved himself capable of doing the impossible, one should not doubt that he can accomplish another.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọgbọọgbọ́n làgbàlagbà-á fi ńsá fún ẹranlá.
english_literal: It is with cunning that a grown man runs away from a bull.
interpretation_gold: A grown person should know how to avoid disaster without losing face.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọjọ́ eré là ńjiyàn ohun.
english_literal: It is on a playful occasion that one argues about matters.
interpretation_gold: Arguments conducted in jest conceal some serious import.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọjọ́ tíìlù-ú bá ńlu onílù, iṣẹ́ mìíràn-án yá.
english_literal: The day the drum begins to beat the drummer is the day he should seek another employment.
interpretation_gold: One should know when to abandon an unprofitable proposition.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọjọ́ tí olówó ńṣẹbọ ni à-wà-jẹ-wà-mu ìwọ̀fà.
english_literal: The day the person who did the hiring makes a sacrifice is the day the hired hand eats and drinks.
interpretation_gold: The poor will eat when the rich provide a feast.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀kẹ́rẹ́ ńsunkún agbádá; èyí tí àjàò-ó dá léṣìí kí ló fi ṣe?Ṣebí igi ló fi ngùn.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: The squirrel weeps for want of a stately garment; the garment the àjàò bird made last year, what did it do with it? Was it not tree climbing it used the garment for?
english_literal: (It is silly to hanker for something one cannot use anyway.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọkọ́ ọlọ́kọ́ la fi ńgbọ́n èkìtì.
english_literal: It is other people's hoe that one uses to clear a mound of rubbish.
interpretation_gold: One is usually more respectful of one's own property than of others'.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan là ńyọ ẹsẹ̀ lábàtà.
english_literal: One at a time is how one extricates one's feet from a mire.
interpretation_gold: The best way to approach a problem is systematically.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Compare Ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan là ńyọ ẹsẹ̀ lábàtà. The following entry is a variant.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan là ńyọ ẹsẹ̀ lẹ́kù.
english_literal: One at a time is how one removes one's legs from a masquerade costume.
interpretation_gold: The best way to approach a problem is systematically.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Compare Ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan là ńyọ ẹsẹ̀ lábàtà.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọkùnrin jẹ́jẹ́ a-bìwà-kunkun.
english_literal: An easy-going man's gentle mien hides a strong disposition.
interpretation_gold: The quiet type is often a tough customer.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọlọ ò lọ ló dé Ìbarà?Ìbarà a máa ṣe ilé ọlọ?

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: If the grindstone did not move, how did it get to Ìbarà? Is Ìbarà the home of grindstones?
english_literal: People do not travel from home without some reason.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọlọ́gbọ́n dorí ẹja mú; òmùgọ́ dìrù-u ẹ̀ mú.
english_literal: The wise person grabs a fish by the head; the fool grabs it by the tail fin.
interpretation_gold: The wise person knows better than a fool the best way to handle a situation.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọlọ́gbọ́n jẹni bí ẹmùrẹ́n; aṣiwèré jẹni bí ìgbọ̀ngbọ̀n.
english_literal: The wise person bites one like a mosquito; the mad person bites one like a gadfly.
interpretation_gold: Cautiousness will get one to one's goal far more successfully than brashness.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọlọgbọ́n ló lè mọ àdììtú èdè.
english_literal: Only a wise person can decipher the meaning of speech.
interpretation_gold: The deep meanings and nuances of an utterance are for the wise only to understand.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọlọgbọ́n ńdẹ ihò, ọ̀mọ̀rànán dúró tì í; ọlọgbọ́n ní “Háà, ó jáde!”Ọ̀mọ̀rán ní “Háà, mo kì í!”Ọlọgbọ́n ní “Kí lo kì?” Ọ̀mọ̀rán ní “Kí nìwọ náà-á ló jáde?”
english_literal: The cunning man is watching a hole, and the knowledgeable person is standing by him; the cunning man exclaims, “Ha, it has sprung out!” The knowledgeable person responds, “Ha, I have grabbed it!” The cunning person asks, “What did you grab?” The knowledgeable person asks in turn, “What did you say sprang out?”
interpretation_gold: Two matched wits are in contest.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọlọgbọ́n ni yó jogún ògo; aṣiwèrè ni yó ru ìtìjú wálé.
english_literal: The wise child will inherit glory; the idiot child will bring shame home with him.
interpretation_gold: A wise child is to be preferred to an idiot.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọlọgbọ́n ọmọ ní ḿmú inú-u bàbá ẹ̀ dùn; aṣiwèrè ọmọ ní ḿba inú ìyá ẹ̀ jẹ́.
english_literal: A wise child gladdens the heart of his father; an imbecile of a child saddens the heart of his mother.
interpretation_gold: Every parent would prefer a wise child to an idiot.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọlọ́jà kì í wípé kọ́jà ó tú.
english_literal: The owner of the market never wishes the market to be disrupted.
interpretation_gold: People always want the best outcome for their ventures.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọlọ́tí kì í mọ ọmọ ẹ̀ lólè
english_literal: The wine seller never realizes that his child is a thief.
interpretation_gold: One is always blind to the flaws of those one loves.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọlọ́tọ̀ọ́ ní tòun ọ̀tọ̀; ìyá ẹ̀-ẹ́ kú nílé, o gbé e lọ sin sóko.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọlọ́tọ̀ says his ways are different; his mother dies at home and he takes her to the farm for burial.
english_literal: (The unconventional person will always do things differently.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọmọ atiro tó ra bàtà fún bàbá ẹ̀, ọ̀rọ̀ ló fẹ́ gbọ́.
english_literal: The child of a cripple who bought shoes for his father is asking for a stern lecture.
interpretation_gold: One must not be thoughtless in one's actions.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọmọ ẹní dàra, bí-i ká fi ṣaya kọ́.
english_literal: One's child may be beautiful, but one cannot make her one's wife.
interpretation_gold: Not all attractive propositions can be pursued.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọmọ ẹni ẹlẹni ò jọ ọmọ ẹni; ọmọ eni ì-bá jiyán, ọmọ ẹni ẹlẹ́ni a jẹ̀kọ.
english_literal: Other people's children are not like one's own; when one's child eats pounded yams, other people's children will eat corn meal loaf.
interpretation_gold: One always favors one's own children over those of others.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọmọ ẹni kì í gbọnsẹ̀ ká fi eèsún nù ú nídìí.
english_literal: One does not, after one's child defecates, wipe the child's anus with the abrasive elephant grass.
interpretation_gold: One does not deliberately injure those who look to one for protection.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọmọ iná là ńrán síná.
english_literal: It is the child of fire that one sends on an errand to fire.
interpretation_gold: It is best to match the remedy to the problem.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: “Ọmọ-ọ̀ mi ò yó” la mọ̀; “ọmọ-ọ̀ mí yó, ṣùgbọ́n kò rí sáárá fẹ́,” a ò mọ ìyẹn.
english_literal: “My child did not have enough to eat,” we understand; “My child had enough to eat but had no snuff to snort,” that we do not understand.
interpretation_gold: People should care for their children, not spoil them with over-indulgence.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọmọ tí ò ní baba kì í jìjà ẹ̀bi.
english_literal: A fatherless child should not engage in an unjust fight.
interpretation_gold: Never provoke trouble unless you have strong backers.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Compare Ọmọ tí ò níyàá kì í dégbò ẹ̀hìn.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọmọdé kékeré ò mọ ogun, ó ní kógun ó wá, ó ní bógún bá dé òun a kó síyàrá ìyá òun.
english_literal: A small child does not know what war is like, hence, he says that war should break out, for when it does he will go hide in his mother's room.
interpretation_gold: Ignorance often leads people to bite off much more than they can chew.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọmọdé kì í mọ àkókò tí kúrò-kúròó fi ńkúrò.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A small child never knows when kúròkúrò takes its leave.
english_literal: (Youth is a stranger to etiquette or protocol.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọmọde kì í mọ ìtàn, kó mọ à-gbọ́-wí, kó mọ ọjọ́ tí a ṣe ẹ̀dá òun.
english_literal: A child does not know so much history and know so much hearsay that it knows the day of its creation.
interpretation_gold: However knowledgeable a youth might be, some deep knowledge would be beyond him.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọmọdé kì í mọ ori-í jẹ kó má rá a lẹ́nu.
english_literal: A child is never so careful about eating corn meal that it does not smear the meal on its mouth.
interpretation_gold: A youth may be clever, but he will inevitably make some mistakes.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọmọdé kì í ní ina níle kí tòde má jòó o.
english_literal: A child does not have fire at home and therefore escape being burned by the fire abroad.
interpretation_gold: Being secure and well respected in one's home does not save one from vicissitudes outside the home.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọmọdé mọ sáárá, ṣùgbọ́n kò mọ àlọ̀yí.
english_literal: A child knows snuff, but does not know how to grind and turn the tobacco.
interpretation_gold: A child is good at consuming, but not at procuring.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọmọdé ní wọ́n ńjẹ igún, bàbá ẹ̀-ẹ́ ní wọn kì í jẹ ẹ́; ó ní ẹnìkán jẹ ẹ́ rí lójú òun; bàbá ẹ̀-ẹ́ ní ta ni? Ó ní ẹni náà ò sí.
english_literal: A child says that people do eat vultures, and its father says people do not; the child says someone did eat a vulture in its presence; its father asks, who? The child says the person is dead.
interpretation_gold: The youth who attempts to challenge the wisdom of the elders will find himself tripped by his own mouth.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọmọdé ò mẹ̀fọ́, ó ńpè é légbògi.
english_literal: A child does not recognize a vegetable and calls it medicine.
interpretation_gold: An uninformed person will inevitably make a fool of him/herself.
notes: Compare the following two entries.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọmọdé ò mọ oògùn, ó ńpè é lẹ́fọ̀o?; kò mọ̀ pé ikú tó pa baba òun ni.
english_literal: A child does not know medicine and he therefore calls it vegetables; it does not recognize it as what killed its father.
interpretation_gold: People may call disasters on their own heads out of ignorance.
notes: Compare the previous and the following entries.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọmọdé ò moògùn ó ńpè é lẹ́gùn-ún.
english_literal: A child does not know medicine and says it is a thorn.
interpretation_gold: The ignorant person knows not the value of anything.
notes: [111] Compare the previous two entries.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọmọdé yìí, máa wò mí lójú, ẹni (tí) a bá lọ sóde là ńwò lójú.
english_literal: Child, keep your eyes on me; one keeps one's eyes on the person who takes one visiting.
interpretation_gold: Always pay attention to what your guide and instructor does and tells you to do.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀mọ̀ràn ní ḿmọ oyún ìgbín.
english_literal: Only a sage knows the pregnancy of a snail.
interpretation_gold: Deep wisdom is the gift of only a select few.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀pá gbóńgbó ní nṣíwájú agbọ́ọni.
english_literal: It is a small walking-stick that goes before the person who walks a path overhung with foliage that is wet with morning dew.
interpretation_gold: One uses the tools or weapons at one's disposal to tackle the challenges that confront one.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọpẹ́ ló yẹ ẹrú.
english_literal: Gratitude is what befits the slave.
interpretation_gold: People should be grateful for whatever charity they receive.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀pẹ̀lẹ̀ èèyàn, bí a ò bá gbé e lulẹ̀, kò níí lè fọhùn ire.
english_literal: A person who is like the divining string: unless you throw him down he will not talk sense.
interpretation_gold: Some people respond only to force.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ ní kéjò máa kálọ; ìjà òún di ojú ọ̀nà.
english_literal: The toad tells the snake to follow it, for it does not fight except by the roadside.
interpretation_gold: Weaklings always make sure that saviors are around before they get into a fight.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ ní òún lè sín ìlẹ̀kẹ̀; ta ní jẹ́ fi ìlẹ̀kẹ̀ ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ sídìí ọmọ-ọ ẹ̀?
english_literal: The toad boasts that it knows how to string beads; who, though, would put a toad's beads around his child's waist?
interpretation_gold: Not just anything will do for discriminating people.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀pọ̀lọ̀ ńyan káńdú-kàǹdù-káńdú lóju ẹlẹ́gùúsí; ẹlẹ́gùúsí ò gbọdọ̀ yí i lata.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: The toad struts nonchalantly before the person cooking ẹ̀gúsí stew; the person cooking the ẹ̀gúsí stew will never add it to the ingredients.
english_literal: (A person outside one's jurisdiction may well taunt one.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀pọ̀lọ́ ò mọ̀nà odò, ó dà á sí àwàdà.
english_literal: The toad does not know the way to the stream and turns matters into a jest.
interpretation_gold: When one is stumped, one covers one's embarrassment with laughter.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ òjò ní ńlé eégún wọlé kẹri-kẹri.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: It is a deluge that chases the eégún masquerader indoors indefinitely.
english_literal: (When problems become overwhelming one has no choice but to succumb to them.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀ràn kan la fi ńṣòfin ọ̀kan.
english_literal: One problem serves as the basis for a law that will apply to another case.
interpretation_gold: Experience serves as a precedence for future occurrences.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀ràn ọlọ́ràn la fi ńkọ́gbọ́n.
english_literal: From other people's problems one learns wisdom.
interpretation_gold: One should learn from other people's vicissitudes.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀ràn tí ò sunwọ̀n, konko ǹṣojú.
english_literal: A matter that is unpalatable hardens the eyes.
interpretation_gold: When one is in the wrong one hides behind braggadocio.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀rọ̀ kì í gbórín ká fi ọ̀bẹ bù ú, ẹnu la fi ńwí i.
english_literal: A problem is not so formidable that one attacks it with a knife; one tackles it with the mouth.
interpretation_gold: The weightiest problem is resolvable through discussion and negotiation.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀rọ̀ la fi ńjẹ omitooro ọ̀rọ̀.
english_literal: Words are the things with which to savor the delicious broth of words.
interpretation_gold: It is with words that one resolves all problems.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀rọ̀-ọ́ ni òun ò nílé; ibi tí wọ́n bá rí ni wọ́n ti ńsọ òun.
english_literal: Discourse says it has no home; people engage in it wherever they please.
interpretation_gold: Any place is a good place for an exchange of views.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀rọ̀ rere ní ńyọ obì lápò; ọ̀rọ̀ búburú ní ńyọ ọfà lápó.
english_literal: Good talk brings the kola-nut out of the pouch; provocative talk draws the arrow out of th quiver.
interpretation_gold: Judicious language defuses problems, while thoughtless talk aggravates them.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀rọ̀ tí ọlọgbọ́n bá sọ, ẹnu aṣiwèrè la ti ńgbọ́ ọ.
english_literal: Whatever a wiseman says will be heard repeated by the nitwit.
interpretation_gold: Romour mongers always distort the news they hear from reliable sources.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀rọ̀ tó dojú rú di ti ọlọ́rọ̀, ayé á dẹ̀hìn.
english_literal: A problem that is too complicated to resolve becomes the sole responsibility of the person concerned; the world leaves him/her to his/her devices.
interpretation_gold: People will help one only so far; in the end each person must confront his/her problems alone.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọsán gbé ojú ọrun le kókó; bó bá wọ odò, a di ọ̀-rọ̀-pọ̀jọ̀-pọ̀jọ̀.
english_literal: The bow-string is taut while it remains on the bow; dipped into the river it becomes very soft indeed.
interpretation_gold: One thrives on one's home ground where conditions are ideal; in hostile territory one becomes helpless.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀sán ọ̀run ò pọ́n; ẹni tó bá yá kó máa bá tiẹ̀ lọ.
english_literal: It is not yet noon time in heaven; whoever is anxious to get there may go ahead by himself/herself.
interpretation_gold: One is not eager to join others in deadly adventures.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọwọ́ aṣiwèrè ni a gbé ḿbá apá yíya.
english_literal: It is in the hands of an imbecile that one finds a severed arm.
interpretation_gold: Simple-minded people do not know how to cover their tracks or get rid of the evidence.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ọ̀wọ̀-ọ kókó la fi ńwọ igi; ọ̀wọ̀ òrìṣà la fi ńwọ àfín.
english_literal: The regard one has for the knob is the one with which one clothes the tree; the regard one has for the gods is the same that one invests the albino with.
interpretation_gold: One extends the same regard one has for certain people to those associated with them.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom

english_literal: [Back to text]
notes: 106. The wine seller leaves his child in charge, and does not realize that he has been cutting it with water. [Back to text]

yoruba: 107. Ọlọ́tọ̀ means “One who is different.”
english_literal: [Back to text]
notes: 108. The assumption, of course, is that the mother has charge of her own children and others'. [Back to text]

english_literal: [Back to text]

english_literal: [Back to text]

english_literal: [Back to text]

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Rà á ire, gà á ire; ìpéǹpéjú ni àlà-a fìlà.
english_literal: Press it well on the head; puff it out; the eyebrow is the limit for the cap.
interpretation_gold: One may be free to use one's possession as one pleases, but there are still some conventions one must observe.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ràdà-ràdà-á mọ ibi tí ó ńrè.
english_literal: The meandering person knows where he is headed.
interpretation_gold: A person may seem without a purpose, but he or she is engaged in some thing known to himself or herself.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Rírí tí a rí igún la fi ńta igún lọ́fà.
english_literal: It is because one sees the vulture that one shoots arrows at it.
interpretation_gold: If one does not make oneself available, one would not present a target for people's hostility.
notes: . Previous Contents Next

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: “Sìn mí ká relé àna,” ó wẹ̀wù ẹtù.
english_literal: “Go with me to my in-laws' home,” and he wore a garment made from rich hand-woven material.
interpretation_gold: Said of a person who attempts to steal other people's glory when he/she is supposed to be helping them.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Sọ̀rọ̀ kí ọlọ́rọ̀ gbọ́, àbùkù ní ńfi kanni.
english_literal: Spreading rumors into the ears of the subject of the rumor brings disgrace to one.
interpretation_gold: One should refrain from rumor mongering.
notes: . Previous Contents Next

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ṣàǹgó kì í jà kó mú ilé aró.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ṣango does not fight and destroy the enclosure for dyeing.
english_literal: (Some people are beyond the reach of some nemesis.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ṣàngó ní òun ní ńkó ọkùnrin suuru bá jà; Èṣù ní bí-i tòun? Ṣàngó ní kí tÈṣù kúrò.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ṣàngó says he gathers people around him to fight together; Èṣù asks if Ṣàngó includes people like him, and Ṣàngó says Èṣù is the exception.
english_literal: (No one wants to engage in any venture with an unpredictable trouble maker.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: “Ṣe mí níṣu” ní ńṣíwájú “ẹ kúuṣẹ́” bí?
english_literal: Does “Give me some yam” go before “Hello there, you working man.”?
interpretation_gold: It is bad form to ask people for favors before you say hello to them.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: This is a variant of “Bùn mi níṣu kan” . . .

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ṣẹ̀kẹ̀rẹ̀ ò ṣéé fọ̀pá na.
english_literal: The beaded musical gourd is not something to play with a stick.
interpretation_gold: Always apply the proper tool to the job.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ṣẹ́kẹ́-ṣẹkẹ̀-ẹ́ dára, ṣùgbọ́n alágbẹ̀dẹ ò rọ ọ́ fún ọmọ ẹ̀.
english_literal: Handcuffs are pretty, but the blacksmith does not fashion them for his own child.
interpretation_gold: When trouble is being distributed, one always wishes to exempt one's own people.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Sútà ò nílé; ìkóríta lÈṣù ńgbé.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Perfidy has no home; the home of Èṣù is the crossroads.
english_literal: (No one makes room in his or her home for an abomination.)
notes: . Previous Contents Next

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ta lèèyàn nínú ẹrú Ààrẹ? A ní Ìdaganna la wá wá, ẹ ní Ìdakolo?

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Which of the Ààrẹ́'s slaves is a person of any account? We said we came looking for Ìdaganna, and you ask, “Ìdakolo?”
english_literal: (Said to indicate that one's auditor is making nonsense out of the sense one is making. Also, there is nothing to choose between two worthless things.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ta ní jẹ́ jẹ ọṣẹ kó fògìrì fọṣọ?
english_literal: Who would eat soap and wash clothes with fermented beans?
interpretation_gold: Who would seek unease when ease is available?

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ta ní mọ̀dí òjò, bí kò ṣe Ṣàngó?

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Who can know the secret of the rain if not Ṣàngo?
english_literal: (Only those privy to mysteries can explain mysterious events.)

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Tábà tí ò dùn, ẹnu ò tà á.
english_literal: Snuff that is not pleasant, the mouth cannot not sell.
interpretation_gold: No amount of talk will make something unpleasant become pleasant.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: “Tèmi ò ṣòro,” tí kì í jẹ kọ́mọ alágbẹ̀dẹ ní idà.
english_literal: “Mine is not urgent.” which prevents the son of the blacksmith from owning a sword.
interpretation_gold: The person who always yields to others will never get anywhere.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Tẹni ní ńjọni lójú; eèrà-á bímọ-ọ ẹ̀ ó sọ ọ́ ní òyírìgbí.
english_literal: One's own thing is what impresses one; the ant has a child and names it The-one-who-rolls-mightily-around.
interpretation_gold: One always tends to overestimate the worth of one's possession.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Tẹni ntẹni; bí àpọ́n bá sun iṣu a bù fọ́mọ-ọ ẹ̀.
english_literal: One's own is one's own; when a man without a wife roasts yams he cuts a piece for his child.
interpretation_gold: One makes do with what one has.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Tẹ̀tẹ́ ní ńṣíwájú eré sísa.
english_literal: A child's learning to walk comes before running.
interpretation_gold: One should observe some order in what one does.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Tìẹ́ sàn, tèmí sàn, lolókùnrùn méjì-í fi ńdìmú.
english_literal: “Your condition is better; My condition is better,” is what gets two invalids into a fight.
interpretation_gold: Fools will fight over the most stupid things.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Tinú ọ̀lẹ lọ̀lẹ ńjẹ; aṣiwèrè èèyàn ni ò mọ èrú tí yó gbà.
english_literal: The lazy person eats the products of his native wisdom; only a fool does not know what devious way will be fruitful.
interpretation_gold: If one lacks industry, one had better be resourceful.
notes: . Previous Contents Next

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Wàrà-wàrà là ńyọ oró iná.
english_literal: When one is on fire one's reaction is extremely agile.
interpretation_gold: One should not delay in exacting vengeance for a wrong.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Compare Wéréwéré lọmọdé ḿbọ oko èèsì.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Wèrè-é dùn-ún wò, kò ṣé-é bí lọ́mọ.
english_literal: An imbecile makes an entertaining spectacle, but one would not want one as one's child.
interpretation_gold: One might be tolerant of simplicity or irresponsibility in other people, but not in one's own relatives.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Wèrè-é yàtọ̀ sí wéré; wéré kì í ṣe wèrè; ìjá yàtọ̀ sí eré.
english_literal: Madness differs from the singing of Islamic songs; the singing of Islamic songs is not madness; fighting is different from playing.
interpretation_gold: One should not confuse jesting with quarrelling.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Wéré-wéré lọmọdé ḿbọ oko èèsì.
english_literal: A child's journey home from a nettle bush is fast indeed.
interpretation_gold: Painful problems enforce quick attention.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Compare Wàrà-wàrà là ńyọ oró iná.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Wò mí lójú, wò mí lẹ́ẹ̀kẹ́; ẹni a bá lọ sóde là ńwò lójú.
english_literal: Keep your eyes on my face, and keep your eyes on my cheeks; one keeps one's eyes on the person with whom one goes visiting.
interpretation_gold: People should not cultivate wandering eyes.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: “Wo ọmọ-ọ̀ mi dè mí”: ó ńlo kíjìpá mẹ́ta gbó; mélòó ni ọlọ́mọ-ọ́ máa lò gbó?
english_literal: “Look after the child for me”: she wears three durable hand-loom wrappers to tatters; how many would the mother of the child herself wear out?
interpretation_gold: The caretaker should not use up all his own resources for the benefit of his/her employer.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Wolé-wolé kì í wolé agbọ́n láì tẹ́.
english_literal: The sanitary inspector does not inspect a wasp's home without coming to grief.
interpretation_gold: One should be cautious in performing one's duties.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Wọ́n ní, “Afọ́jú, o ò tanná alẹ́.” Ó ní àtọ̀sán àtòru, èwo lòún rí níbẹ?
english_literal: People said, “Blind man, you did not light a lamp.” He asked, night or day, which one would his eyes register?
interpretation_gold: One should not waste one's efforts in procuring things one cannot use.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Wọ́n ní, “Afọ́jú, ọmo-ọ̀ ẹ-ẹ́ pẹran.” Ó ní kò dá òun lójú, àfi bí òún bá tọ́ ọ wò.
english_literal: They said to the blind man, “Blind man, you son has killed a game.” He responds that he cannot believe them until he has tasted the meat.
interpretation_gold: Always insist on proof positive.
notes: . Previous Contents

yoruba: A bu omi lámù a rí eégún; kí ni ẹni tó lọ sódò lọ pọnmi yó rìí?
english_literal: We scoop water from the water pot and see a masquerader; what will the person who goes to draw water at the river find?
interpretation_gold: If a person exposed to minimal risk cries disaster, what would the person exposed to much greater risk do?

yoruba: A fún ọ níṣu lỌ́yọ̀ọ́ ò ńdúpẹ́; o rígi sè é ná?
You are given yams at Ọyọ and you rejoice; have you secured wood to cook them?
english_literal: (Never assume that a propitious beginning assures a successful conclusion.)

yoruba: A ki ẹsẹ̀ kan bọ odò omi fà á; bí a bá wá ti mejèèjì bọ́ ọ́ ńkọ́?
english_literal: One dips one leg into the stream and the water tugs at it; what if one had dipped both legs into it?
interpretation_gold: Repercussions should not be disproportionate to the act.

yoruba: A kì í bá ẹlẹ́nu jìjà òru.
english_literal: One does not fight at night with a braggart.
interpretation_gold: Never get into a competition with a braggart unless a witness is present.

yoruba: A kì í bú ọba onígẹ̀gẹ̀ lójú àwọn èèyàn-án ẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not insult a king with a goitre in the presence of his people.
interpretation_gold: Never expose yourself to repercussions with careless speech or indiscreet behavior.

yoruba: A kì í du orí olórí kí àwòdì gbé tẹni lọ.
english_literal: One does not fight to save another person's head only to have a kite carry one's own away.
interpretation_gold: One should not save other's at the cost of one's own safety.

yoruba: A kì í fi ìkánjú lá ọbẹ̀ gbígbóná.
english_literal: One does not eat scalding stew in a hurry.
interpretation_gold: Patience is best in delicate or difficult matters.

yoruba: A kì í gbélé gba ọfá láìlọ ogun.
english_literal: One does not sit at home, not go to war, and yet be shot with an arrow.
interpretation_gold: One should be safe in one's own home.

yoruba: A kì í kánjú tu olú-ọrán; igba ẹ̀ ò tó-ó sebẹ̀.
One does not gather olú-ọrán mushrooms in haste; two hundred of them are not enough to make a stew.
english_literal: (Certain tasks demand patience if they are to come out right.)

yoruba: A kì í rídìí òkun; a kì í rídìí ọsà; ọmọ-oní-gele-gele kì í jẹ́ kí wọ́n rídìí òun.
english_literal: One never sees the bottom of the ocean; no one ever sees the bottom of the lagoon; a well-bred woman will never expose her buttocks to anyone.
interpretation_gold: People should not expose their innermost secrets to all and sundry.

yoruba: A kì í rójú ẹni purọ́ mọ́ni.
english_literal: One does not look into the eyes of a person and still tell a lie against that person.
interpretation_gold: It is always easier to do evil to people when they are absent.

yoruba: A kì í sọ̀rọ̀ orí bíbẹ́ lójú ọmọdé; lọ́rùnlọ́rùn ni yó máa wo olúwa-a ẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not speak of a beheading in the presence of a child; otherwise his gaze will be fixated on the neck of the person concerned.
interpretation_gold: Never discuss a secret in the hearing of a person whose behavior will give the secret away.

yoruba: À ńgba òròmọ adìẹ lọ́wọ́ ikú, ó ní wọn ò jẹ́ kí òun jẹ̀ láàtàn.
english_literal: One struggles to save the chick from certain death, and it complains that one is preventing it from foraging at the dump.
interpretation_gold: Chicks foraging at the dump are easy prey for kites.

yoruba: A níṣẹ́ iṣẹ́ ẹ, o ní ò ńlọ sóko; bó o bá lọ sóko ò ḿbọ̀ wá bá a nílé.
english_literal: You are told that a job is your responsibility and you say you are on your way to the farm; you may be on your way to the farm, but the job will be there on your return.
interpretation_gold: One may devise stratagems to defer carrying out one's duties, but they are unlikely to make others carry them out.

yoruba: À ńṣa kẹ́kẹ́, aájò ẹwà ni; à ḿbàbàjà, aájò ẹwà ni.
Marking one's face with kẹ́kẹ́ is a quest for beauty; marking one's face with àbàjà is a quest for beauty.
interpretation_gold: The pains one takes to adorn oneself are for a good end.

yoruba: A sìnkú tán, alugba ò lọ; ó fẹ́ ṣúpó ni?
english_literal: The funeral is over, but the calabash beater does not take his leave; does he want to inherit a wife?
interpretation_gold: This proverb has the same import as, A kúnlẹ̀, a pàgbò . . .

yoruba: Abẹ ní ḿbẹ orí; oníṣẹ́ àtẹ́lẹsẹ̀ ní ḿbẹ ọ̀nà; bèbè ìdí ní ḿbẹ kíjìpá; bí a dáwọ́-ọ bíbẹni, a tán nínú ẹni.
english_literal: The razor begs the scalp; the wayfarer's soles beg the path; waist beads beg the home-woven cloth; when the begging is done, one lets matters drop.
interpretation_gold: It is a person that is close to one that placates one; after such placation, one allows oneself to be appeased.

yoruba: Abẹ́rẹ́ bọ́ sómi táló; Ọ̀dọ̀fín ní òun-ún gbọ́ “jàbú!”
The needle makes an almost inaudible sound when it drops into the water; Ọdọfin said he heard a loud splash.
english_literal: (Excessive exaggeration amounts to lying.)

yoruba: Abiyamọ, kàgbo wàrà; ọjọ́ ńlọ.
english_literal: Nursing mother, make the herbal decoction in good time; the day is waning.
interpretation_gold: Attend to duties in time.

yoruba: Àbùlẹ̀ ní ḿmú aṣọ tọ́; ẹni tí kò tọ́jú àbùlẹ̀ yó ṣe ara-a ẹ̀ lófò aṣọ.
english_literal: Patching extends the life of clothes; whoever does not save materials for patching deprives himself or herself of clothing.
interpretation_gold: Everything has its use; conserve your resources.

yoruba: Àdàbà ńpògèdè, ó rò pé ẹyẹlé ò gbọ́; ẹyẹlé gbọ́, títiiri ló tiiri.
english_literal: The dove recites incantations, thinking that the pigeon cannot hear; the pigeon hears; it is only pretending to sleep.
interpretation_gold: Never mistake a person's easygoing demeanor for cowardice or folly.

yoruba: Adìẹ́ ńjẹkà, ó ḿmumi, ó ńgbé òkúta pẹ́-pẹ̀-pẹ́ mì, ó ní òun ò léhín; ìdérègbè tó léhín ńgbé irin mì bí?
english_literal: The chicken eats corn, drinks water, even swallows small pebbles, and yet complains that it lacks teeth; does the goat that has teeth swallow steel?
interpretation_gold: One should be content with one's lot.

yoruba: Àdó gba ara ẹ̀ tẹ́lẹ̀, ká tó fi oògùn sí?
english_literal: Could the small gourd save itself, before we put charms into it?
interpretation_gold: Do not seek protection from a helpless person.

yoruba: Àdóìṣí loògùn ọrọ̀.
english_literal: Choosing-a-base-and-maintaining-it is the medicine for wealth.
interpretation_gold: One should not be a rolling stone.

yoruba: Afẹ́fẹ́ tó wọlé tó kó aṣọ iyàrá, ìkìlọ̀ ni fún ẹni tó wọ tiẹ̀ sọrùn.
english_literal: The wind that enters into the house and carries off the clothes in the bedroom is a warning to those who wear theirs around their necks.
interpretation_gold: When disaster befalls the most formidable people, those less formidable should take warning.

yoruba: Àfojúdi ìlẹ̀kẹ̀ ní ńjẹ́ “Ẹrú-kò-ní.”
english_literal: It is an impertinent bead that is named “The-slave-does-not-own-its like.”
interpretation_gold: One must be mindful of how one's actions might affect others.

yoruba: Àgékù ejò, tí ńṣoro bí agbọ́n.
english_literal: Partially severed snake, that stings like a wasp.
interpretation_gold: A wounded adversary is a vicious one.

yoruba: Àgúnbàjẹ́ ni tolódó.
english_literal: Pounding-until-it-is-ruined is the habit of the owner of the mortar.
interpretation_gold: One should exercise restraint in using what has in abundance.

yoruba: Àgùntàn bọ̀lọ̀jọ̀ ò gbàgbé eléèrí bọ̀rọ̀.
english_literal: The big, fat sheep does not soon forget the provider of corn bran.
interpretation_gold: One remembers one's benefactor.

yoruba: Àgùntàn ńwò sùn-ùn; ọgbọ́n inú pé egbèje.
english_literal: The sheep stares blankly, but its cunning stratagems number a thousand four hundred.
interpretation_gold: Looks are deceptive.

yoruba: Àgùntàn ò jí ní kùtùkùyù ṣe ẹnu bọbọ.
english_literal: A sheep does not wake in the morning and droop its mouth.
interpretation_gold: One should not dawdle in the morning.

yoruba: Àgbà òṣìkà ńgbin ìyà sílẹ̀ de ọmọ-ọ rẹ̀.
english_literal: A wicked elder sows suffering for his children.
interpretation_gold: One's character often affects the fortunes of one's children.

yoruba: Compare, Àgbà tó gbin èbù ìkà . . .
Àgbẹ̀ ò dáṣọ lóṣù, àfọdún.
english_literal: A farmer does not make new clothes monthly, only annually.
interpretation_gold: The reward for one's labor is often a long time coming.

yoruba: Àgbẹ̀ tó bá pẹ́ nílé ò níí kọ oko ọ̀sán.
english_literal: A farmer who tarries in the house will not object to hoeing the farm in the afternoon.
interpretation_gold: He who dallies makes his tasks that much more difficult.

yoruba: À-gbẹ́rù-àì-wẹ̀hìn lọ̀pálábá fi gbàgbé ìyá ẹ̀ sílẹ̀.
english_literal: Picking-up-one's-load-without-checking-one's-rear caused the piece of broken bottle to forget its mother on the ground.
interpretation_gold: The broken bottle suffered its fate, perhaps, because it was not careful about what it “carried.” The hasty traveller leaves his goods behind.

yoruba: Agbójúlógún fi ara-a rẹ̀ fóṣì ta.
english_literal: He-who-places-his-hopes-on-inheritance delivers himself to destitution.
interpretation_gold: One should secure one's own living.

yoruba: Àgbọ́ká etí ọlọ́ràn á di.
english_literal: The ear that will insist on hearing everything will go deaf.
interpretation_gold: There is some benefit to ignoring certain things.

yoruba: Àgbọ́kànlé ò pani lébi.
english_literal: A thing in which one reposes one's trust does not make one hunger.
interpretation_gold: One's reserve guarantees one's supplies.

yoruba: Àìfẹ̀sọ̀ké ìbòsí ni kò ṣéé gbè.
english_literal: It is an alarm that is raised without moderation that finds no helpers.
interpretation_gold: If the person who raises an alarm puts people off by his or her methods, they will not come to his or her aid.

yoruba: Àìgbọ́ràn, baba àfojúdi.
english_literal: Disobedience, father of disregard.
interpretation_gold: To disobey people is to show a lack of regard for them.

yoruba: Àìlèfọhùn ní ńṣáájú orí burúkú.
english_literal: Inability to speak out precedes misfortunes.
interpretation_gold: A person who will not speak out on his or her own behalf suffers the consequences.

yoruba: Àìrọ́rọ̀sọ ìyàwó tó wí pé èkúté-ilé yó jẹ idẹ; bẹ́ẹ̀ni Mọ́jidẹ nìyálé-e rẹ̀ ńjẹ́.

The junior wife could find nothing to say, and said that the mice in the house will eat brass; the senior wife if the household happens to be named Mọjidẹ(Ọmọ-ọ́-jẹ-idẹ) (meaning “Child eats brass.”)
english_literal: (Veiled insults directed at an adversary are as potent as any other sort of provocation.)

yoruba: Àìsàn là ńwò, a kì í wo ikú.
english_literal: One treats an illness; one does not treat death.
interpretation_gold: If one neglects an illness until death intervenes, the treatment comes too late.

yoruba: Àìtètèmólè, olèé mólóko.
english_literal: Because of the delay in apprehending the thief, the thief apprehends the owner of the farm.
interpretation_gold: One must be alert in dealing with slippery people; otherwise they turn the tables on one.

yoruba: Ajá ilé ò mọdẹẹ́ ṣe.
english_literal: A domesticated dog does not know how to hunt.
interpretation_gold: Pampering kills initiative.

yoruba: Ajá kì í dán-nu “Kò séwu” lókò ẹkùn.
english_literal: A dog does not boast “No danger” in a leopard's bush.
interpretation_gold: Never sneer at obvious danger.

yoruba: Ajá tí yó sọnù kì í gbọ́ fèrè ọdẹ.
english_literal: A dog destined to be lost does not hear the hunter's whistle.
interpretation_gold: No matter what help one may render, one cannot save an ill-fated person.

yoruba: Ajá tó rí mọ́tò tó dúró fi ara-a ẹ̀ bọ Ògún.
english_literal: A dog that sees a motor vehicle and stands in its was makes itself a sacrifice to Ogun.
interpretation_gold: A person who needlessly endangers him/herself deserves his/her fate.

yoruba: Àjànàkú tí a gbẹ́ ọ̀fìn sílẹ̀ dè, erin-ín mojú; erin ò bá ibẹ̀ lọ.
english_literal: One digs a pit in the path of the elephant, but the elephant can read signs; the elephant does not go that way.
interpretation_gold: The alert person will thwart an enemy's machinations.

yoruba: Àjẹ́ ńké, òkùnrùn ò paradà; ó lówó ẹbọ nílé.
english_literal: A witch proclaims her presence and an invalid does not make away; he must have money for sacrifices at home.
interpretation_gold: One needs not fear a scourge for which one has the remedy.

yoruba: Ajẹnifẹ́ni, èkúté ilé.
english_literal: One-that-bites-and-blows-on-the-wound, the house-mouse.
interpretation_gold: One should be wary of adversaries who pose as friends.

yoruba: Aaka ò gbé ọ̀dàn; igbó ní ńgbé.
english_literal: The hedgehog does not live in the grassland, only in the forest.
interpretation_gold: Certain things are proper; certain things are not.

yoruba: Àkàlàmàgbò-ó ṣoore ó yọ gẹ̀gẹ̀ lọ́rùn.
english_literal: The ground hornbill did a favor and developed a goitre.
interpretation_gold: One's good deeds sometimes come back to haunt one.

yoruba: Compare: Oore tígún ṣe tó fi pá lórí . . .
Akánjú jayé, ọ̀run wọn ò pẹ́.
english_literal: People who live impatiently: their going to heaven is not far off.
interpretation_gold: Reckless living leads to early death.

yoruba: Àáké tí ńgégi-í kọsẹ̀, gbẹ́nàgbẹ́nà-á bu ètù sórí.
english_literal: The axe that cuts wood stumbles, and the carver anoints his head with medicinal powder.
interpretation_gold: The evil doer's conscience will not let him/her rest.

yoruba: Àkèekèé ò ṣé-é dì níbò.
english_literal: A scorpion is not a thing to close one's palms on.
interpretation_gold: Some matters call for extreme caution.

yoruba: Àkèekèé rìn tapótapó.
english_literal: The scorpion travels accompanied by venom.
interpretation_gold: The stalwart is never unprepared to answer a call.

yoruba: Àkèekèé ta Kindo lẹpọ̀n, ará ilée Labata ńrojú; kí ló kàn án níbẹ̀?
english_literal: A scorpion stung Kindo in the testicle, and a person from Labata's household frowns in dismay; what business is it of his?
interpretation_gold: One should not take on matters that are not one's business.

yoruba: Akóbáni lèkúté-ilé; ejò kì í jàgbàdo.
english_literal: The mouse is a bringer of disaster to the innocent; snakes do not eat corn.
interpretation_gold: Bad company brings bad fortune.

yoruba: Àkọ̀ tó bá bá ọ̀bẹ dìtẹ̀ á gbọgbẹ́ láti inú.
english_literal: A sheath that engages in a dispute with a knife will suffer an internal wound.
interpretation_gold: Never court the anger of a person in a position to inflict injury on you.

yoruba: Àlá tí ajá bá lá, inú ajá ní ńgbé.
english_literal: Whatever dream the dog dreams remains inside the dog.
interpretation_gold: Keep your own counsel.

yoruba: Alágbàró ò yege; aláṣọ á gbà á bó dọ̀la.
english_literal: She who borrows a wrapper-skirt to wear is not home free; the owner of the cloth will take it back come tomorrow.
interpretation_gold: There is nothing like having one's own.

yoruba: Aláǹgbá tó fojú di erè, ikùn ejò ni yó bàá ara-a ẹ̀.
english_literal: A lizard that views a python with disregard will find itself in the belly of the snake.
interpretation_gold: Whoever disdains obvious danger will suffer dire consequences.

yoruba: Alápàáǹdẹ̀dẹ̀ ńjayé lébé-lébé.
english_literal: The sparrow enjoys life carefully.
interpretation_gold: The best way to live is carefully.

yoruba: Alára ò lè wí pé kò dun òun, ká ní ó kú àìsùn, ó kú àìwo.
english_literal: The owner of the body does not say that he is in no pain, while we insist on commiserating with him for his sleeplessness and his restlessness.
notes: (One does not commiserate with a person who does not admit his/her misfortune).

yoruba: Alárìnjó tí yó jòó, kó ti ìwòyí mú ẹsẹ̀ kó le kó kó kó.
english_literal: The person who will engage in itinerant dancing should look to his legs in good time.
interpretation_gold: Before embarking on a trade, one should hone one's tools.

yoruba: Aláàárù kì í sọ pé kí ajé ṣe òun pa; ẹlẹ́rù ńkọ́?
english_literal: The hired carrier does not ask to die from his efforts; what would the owner of the merchandise ask?
interpretation_gold: One should not assume other people's responsibilities and risks.

yoruba: Aláwàdà ló lè ṣọkọ òṣónú; ẹni tí kò lẹ́nu mímú tete ò lè ṣọkọ alápẹpẹ.
english_literal: Only a good-humored person can make a good husband for an ill-humored woman; a person whose mouth is not sharp cannot make a good husband for a hyperactive woman.
interpretation_gold: Incompatible natures cannot make a good marriage.

yoruba: Àlejò tó wọ̀ nílé-e Pọ́ngilá, Pọ́ngilá ní, “Ìwọ ta ni?” Àlejò-ó ní òun Bugijẹ; Pọ́ngilá ni, “Tòò, lọ́ dájú igi-i tìrẹ lọ́tọ̀.”

The visitor “who” arrived at the home of Pọngila (Lickwood), Pọngila asked him, “Who are you?”  The visitor replied, “I am Bugijẹ” (Bitewood). Pọngila said, “Well, you had better go find yourself some wood elsewhere.
english_literal: (Do not encourage people to take advantage of you or abuse your generosity.)

yoruba: Àlọ ti alábaun; àbọ̀ ti àna-a rẹ̀.
english_literal: To Tortoise belongs the outward trip; to his father-in-law belongs the return.
interpretation_gold: The person in the right in a dispute, if he/she is too vindictive, quickly becomes the one in the wrong.

yoruba: Àlùkẹrẹsẹ ò mọ̀ pé olóko-ó ládàá.
english_literal: The weed did not know that the farmer had a machete.
interpretation_gold: The evil doer does not consider the response of the person wronged.

yoruba: Àmọ̀jù là ḿmọ ẹkùn-un Sàárẹ́.
english_literal: Saare always goes too far in his description of a leopard.
interpretation_gold: An immoderate display of knowledge soon backfires.

yoruba: Àpáàdì ló tó ko iná lójú.
english_literal: Only a potsherd has what it takes to confront live coal.
interpretation_gold: Only a person capable of confronting a situation should take it on.

yoruba: Apatapara-á pa ara-a rẹ̀ lájùbà; ẹni tí yó ko là ńwòye.
english_literal: Apatapara kills himself in the wilderness; who will carry him is now the question.
interpretation_gold: One should not to outstrip one's help.

yoruba: Àpò tí a kò fi ọwọ́ ẹni dá ṣòro-ó kiwọ́ bọ̀.
english_literal: A pocket one did not make with one's own hand is a difficult one to dip one's hand into.
interpretation_gold: One should keep one's hands to one's own pockets.

yoruba: Ará Ìbàdàn kì í ságun; à ó rìn sẹ́hìn ni wọ́n ńwí.
english_literal: Ibadan people do not run from war; what they say is, “We will fall back a little.”
interpretation_gold: There are ways of avoiding battle without seeming to do so.

yoruba: À-rí-ì-gbọdọ̀-wí, à-rí-ì-gbọdọ̀-fọ̀ ni ikú awo.
english_literal: Something-seen-but-unmentionable, something-seen-but-unspeakable is the death of a guardian of the mysteries.
interpretation_gold: The eyes sometimes see things that are too sacred for the mouth to mention.

yoruba: Àrísá iná, àkòtagìrì ejò; àgbà tó réjò tí kò sá, ara ikú ló ńyá a.
english_literal: Fire, something-one-sees-and-flees, snake, something one sees and jumps; an elder who sees a snake and does not flee flirts with death.
interpretation_gold: Fire and snakes are not things to take lightly; and elder should not be embarrasses to flee from danger.

yoruba: Àròkàn ní ḿmú à-sun-ùn-dá wá; ẹlẹ́kún sunkún ẹ̀ ó lọ.
english_literal: Going-from-one-sadthought-to-another results in endless weeping; the person weeping does his weeping and departs.
interpretation_gold: If one keeps thinking sad thoughts one will ever remain miserable; if one must be sad, one must observe some limits.

yoruba: Arọ ò nasẹ̀ kan dí ọ̀nà.
english_literal: A cripple does not block the road with his legs.
interpretation_gold: A person with a handicap should not challenge those who are not handicapped.

yoruba: Arọ tí kò lẹ́sẹ̀ nílẹ̀-ẹ́ lọ́gbọ́n nínú.
english_literal: A cripple who has no legs to stand on has wisdom inside him.
interpretation_gold: Whatever handicaps one might have, one will have some asset.

yoruba: Arọ́basá ò ṣojo.
english_literal: He-who-flees-on-seeing-the-king is no coward.
interpretation_gold: One's safest course is to steer clear of those in authority.

yoruba: Compare A kì í bọ́ba pàlà kọ́kọ́ ọba má ṣàáni lẹ́sẹ̀.
Arúgbó ṣoge rí; àkísà-á lògbà rí.
english_literal: The old person was once a dandy; the rag was once in fashion.
interpretation_gold: Those who are favored should remember that times and circumstances do change.

yoruba: Àrùn là ńwó a kì í wokú.
english_literal: One treats a disease; one does not treat death.
notes: (We should attend to problems before they become unmanageable.

yoruba: Asárétete ní ńkọjá ilé; arìngbẹ̀rẹ̀ ni yóò rí oyè jẹ.
english_literal: The fast runner will run past his home; the leisurely stroller is the one who will win the title.
interpretation_gold: A fast start does not guarantee success.

yoruba: Compare: Arìngbẹ̀rẹ̀ ni yó mùú oyè délé . . .
Àṣá ḿbá ẹyẹlé ṣeré, ẹyẹlé ńyọ̀; ẹyẹlé ńfikú ṣeré.
english_literal: The kite plays with the pigeon and the pigeon rejoices; the pigeon is courting death.
interpretation_gold: An enemy who pretends friendship is so much more dangerous.

yoruba: Àṣàyá kì í jẹ́ kí ọmọ ọ̀yà ó gbọ́n.
english_literal: Roughhousing keeps the young of the cane rat from learning wisdom.
interpretation_gold: A person who takes life as a jest does not learn to be wary.

yoruba: Àṣesílẹ̀ làbọ̀wábá; ẹni tó da omi síwájú á tẹlẹ̀ tútù.
english_literal: What one puts aside is what one returns to find; whoever dumps water ahead of him/her will step on wet earth.
interpretation_gold: One reaps what one sows.
notes: This is a variant of the previous entry.

yoruba: Àṣẹ̀ṣẹ̀wọ́n ológbò ní ńjìyà; bó bá pẹ́ títí a tó eku-ú pa.
english_literal: Only the newly weaned cat suffers; eventually it will learn to kill mice.
interpretation_gold: A child may be helpless today, but not in the future.

yoruba: Aṣòroówọ̀ bí ẹ̀wù àṣejù.
english_literal: Difficult-to-wear like the garment of immoderation.
interpretation_gold: Wearing the cloak of immoderation exposes one to difficulties.

yoruba: Ata-á kéré; ìjá jù ú.
english_literal: Pepper is small; its fight is much bigger.
interpretation_gold: One should not judge people by their size.

yoruba: Atàkò fọ́ ẹyin àparò; ohun ojú ńwá lojú ńrí.
english_literal: Person-who-stones-and-breaks-partridge's-eggs; the eyes find what the eyes seek.
interpretation_gold: The culprit is asking for trouble, and he will not be disappointed.

yoruba: Ataare-é rẹ́ni tún ìdí-i rẹ̀ ṣe ó ńfi òbùró ṣẹ̀sín; òbùró ìbá rẹ́ni tún ìdí-i rẹ̀ ṣe a sunwọ̀n jú ataare lọ.
Alligator pepper has someone to tend it and it mocks the òbùró tree; had the òbùró tree someone to tend it it would look better than alligator pepper.
english_literal: (A person enjoying a run of good fortune should not deride the less fortunate; if they had been similarly favored there is no telling what they might have accomplished.)

yoruba: Atẹ̀hìnrọ́gbọ́n agétí ajá; a gé e létí tán ó fabẹ pamọ́.
english_literal: A-creature-that-learns-wisdom-in-reverse-order, dog-with-severed-ears; after its ears have been severed it hides the razor.
interpretation_gold: Prevention makes sense only before the disaster.

yoruba: Àtẹ́lẹwọ́ ẹni kì í tanni.
english_literal: One's palm does not deceive one.
interpretation_gold: One's trust is best placed in one's own resources.

yoruba: 1e   Atọrọohungbogbolọ́wọ́Ọlọ́run kì í kánjú.
english_literal: The-seeker-of-all-things-from-God does not yield to impatience.
interpretation_gold: The supplicant must be patient for an answer.

yoruba: Àwòfín ní ḿmú ọ̀rẹ́ bàjẹ́; fírí là ńwo ẹni tí ńwoni.
english_literal: Persistent-staring ruins a friendship; one looks only glancingly at those looking at one.
interpretation_gold: A battle of looks does not help a friendship.

yoruba: See: Àwòfín mú ọ̀rẹ́ bàjẹ́; . . . .
Àáyá kan-án bẹ̀ ọ́ wò; igba wọ́n ti rí ọ.
english_literal: If a single Colubus monkey sees you, be sure that two hundred of them have seen you.
interpretation_gold: A secret that one discloses to one person is as good as published for all.

yoruba: Ayáraròhìn, aya ọdẹ, ó ní ọkọ òun-ún pa èkínní, ó pa ẹ̀kẹfà.
english_literal: The-impatient-reporter, wife of the hunter, she says that her husband killed the first and killed the sixth.
interpretation_gold: The impatient reporter is liable to outstrip her report.

yoruba: Àyé gba ògùnmọ̀ ó ránṣẹ́ sí òdú; àyé gba Tápà ó kọ́lé ìgunnu.
english_literal: The cultivated vegetable is contented, so it sends for its wild variety; the Nupe (Fulani) person is so comfortable that he builds a tall house.
interpretation_gold: When one enjoys a life of ease, one is tempted to overreach.

yoruba: Ayé ò ṣéé fipá jẹ.
english_literal: Life is nothing to enjoy heedlessly.
interpretation_gold: Life demands caution.

The proverb is based on a folktale in which Tortoise stole yams from the farm of its father-in-law. The latter caught Tortoise and tied it up by the path, where people going to their farms saw it and justified the father-in-law. yoruba: 14. The story behind the proverb is of a boy, Sàar;ẹ who ran home panting because he had seen a leopard in the forest. Grateful that the animal did not kill his son, the father killed a cock as a sacrifice.  The boy went on to describe how huge the animal was, and the father, even more thankful, killed a he-goat for sacrifice.  Then the son spoke of how the animal went from okro plant to okro plant to eat the fruits.  The father knew, of course, that only antelopes ate okro, and he scolded the son for not killing the game and bringing it home.
